definition_zh: 普遍的；流行的；盛行的
definition_en: existing widely, common in a place, group or period, or currently dominant
core_image: 街角每家店铺都挂着同一款式的风铃，风一吹整条街都在响
scene: 这里指「普遍的」。 The belief is prevalent among first-year students.
sceneCN: 这里 prevalent 是「普遍的、流行的」（第 1 个义项：在人群中广泛存在）；句意：这种看法在一年级学生中很普遍。图中可辨识物件：连成排的店铺、同款风铃、被风吹起的一片铃声。

pos.zh: 普遍的；流行的；盛行的

senses.title: Common in a group
senses.titleCN: 普遍的：在这群人中到处都有
senses.definition: found widely among the members of a particular group
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定群体的成员中广泛存在
senses.example: The fear of public speaking is prevalent among new teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 害怕当众讲话在新教师中很普遍。
senses.why: prevalere means 'to be stronger, prevail'. What prevails over a group is found throughout it, so the adjective describes wide presence.
senses.whyCN: prevalere 意为“更强、占优势”。在一群人中占优势的东西遍布其中，因此形容词描述“广泛存在”。

senses.title: Dominant opinion
senses.definition: currently accepted or believed by most people, whether or not it is correct
senses.definitionCN: 当前被多数人接受或相信的，无论是否正确
senses.example: The prevalent view was that the climate would not change.
senses.exampleCN: 当时占上风的看法是气候不会改变。
senses.why: The word reports strength of acceptance, not truth. A prevalent error is still prevalent.
senses.whyCN: 这个词报告的是被接受的程度，不是真伪。普遍的错误依然“普遍”。

senses.title: Medical frequency
senses.titleCN: 医学上的常见：病例很多
senses.definition: describing a disease or condition that affects a large share of a population
senses.definitionCN: 描述影响大量人口的疾病或状况
senses.example: The disease is prevalent in areas without clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病在没有清洁水源的地区很常见。
senses.why: Public health uses the adjective where prevalence is high: the condition is not rare, so it changes policy.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生在患病率高时用这个形容词：该状况不罕见，因此会影响政策。

senses.title: Dominant wind or weather
senses.titleCN: 主导风向：常刮的那一股
senses.definition: in meteorology, describing the wind direction most often recorded in an area
senses.definitionCN: 气象学上描述某地出现最多的风向
senses.example: The prevalent wind in July comes from the southwest.
senses.exampleCN: 七月的主导风来自西南。
senses.why: Weather statistics use prevalence as frequency dominance: the direction that prevails is the one that comes most often.
senses.whyCN: 气象统计把“普遍”当作“频率占优”：占上风的风向就是出现最多的那个。

senses.title: Prevailing custom
senses.titleCN: 盛行的习俗：多数人这么做
senses.definition: describing a practice or custom that most people in a society follow
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个社会中多数人遵循的做法或习俗
senses.example: Early marriage was prevalent in the village a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 一个世纪前，早婚在这个村子里很盛行。
senses.why: Customs spread by imitation, so the social version of the word measures how many people copy a behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 习俗靠模仿传播，所以这个词的社会版本度量“有多少人照着做”。

senses.title: Commonest form
senses.titleCN: 最常见的形态：多数属于这一类
senses.definition: describing the most frequent type or variant within a category
senses.definitionCN: 描述某一类别中最常见的类型或变体
senses.example: The prevalent form of the gene differs by region.
senses.exampleCN: 该基因的常见形态随地区而异。
senses.why: Biology counts variants, so prevalent marks the variant with the largest share rather than with the greatest power.
senses.whyCN: 生物学统计变体，所以 prevalent 标记占比最大的那一种，而非最强的那一种。

senses.title: Legal 'prevailing' party
senses.titleCN: 法律上的胜诉方（相关用法）
senses.definition: in legal usage, the related participle prevailing describes the side that wins; prevalent itself means common
senses.definitionCN: 法律用语中相关分词 prevailing 指胜诉一方，而 prevalent 本身意为“普遍”
senses.example: The prevailing party may recover costs.
senses.exampleCN: 胜诉方可以收回诉讼费用。
senses.why: The two forms split: prevailing keeps the courtroom sense of winning, while prevalent keeps the statistical sense of being common.
senses.whyCN: 两个形式分工：prevailing 保留法庭上“胜出”的义，prevalent 保留统计上“常见”的义。

senses.title: Contrast with rare
senses.definition: occupying the high end of a frequency scale, opposed to rare or uncommon
senses.definitionCN: 处在频率刻度的高端，与罕见、少见相对
senses.example: Such storms are prevalent in autumn but rare in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的风暴在秋季常见，在春季罕见。
senses.why: A scale needs both ends. Prevalent is only meaningful against rare, which is why the two words so often appear together.
senses.whyCN: 刻度需要两端。prevalent 只有与“罕见”对照才有意义，所以两词常一起出现。

intro.en: Prevalent is the adjective from Latin praevalere 'to be stronger, prevail' (prae- 'before, beyond' + valere 'be strong'), with the ending -ent from Latin -ent-.
intro.cn: prevalent 是拉丁 praevalere“更强、占优势”（prae-“在前、超过”+ valere“强壮”）的形容词形式，词尾 -ent 来自拉丁 -ent-。

items.en: valere meant 'to be strong, be well, be worth'. It also gives value and valid, so the family is about strength and worth, not about quantity.
items.cn: valere 意为“强壮、健康、有价值”。它还产出 value 与 valid，因此这个词族关乎力量与价值，不关乎数量。

items.en: prae- 'beyond' plus valere gives 'to be stronger than'. The verb first meant winning, then holding sway generally.
items.cn: prae-“超过”加 valere 得“强过”。动词先指取胜，后泛指占据优势。

items.en: the present participle praevalens 'prevailing' became the adjective source for English prevalent.
items.cn: 现在分词 praevalens“占优势的”成为英语 prevalent 的形容词来源。

items.en: English adopts prevalent in the 1500s, first for something having great force or influence, then for something widespread.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪采用 prevalent，先指“有强大力量或影响”，后指“广泛存在”。

items.en: Modern usage fixes the quantitative sense: a prevalent disease is one with many existing cases.
items.cn: 现代用法固定了数量义：“常见病”就是现有病例很多。

items.en: In ordinary speech prevalent now simply means common, and its natural partner is rare.
items.cn: 在日常口语中，prevalent 现在就是“常见”，它的天然搭档是“罕见”。

note.en: The look-alike group shares val- or the pre- prefix; the near-meaning group all say 'common', differing in tone and scale.
note.cn: 形近组共享 val- 或 pre- 前缀；近义组都表“常见”，差别在语气与尺度。

entries.definition: the fact of being widespread or the measured rate. The noun names the state; the adjective describes the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 普遍存在或测得的比率。名词命名状态，形容词描述事物。

entries.definition: current, dominant, or winning. It often modifies wind, opinion or a legal party, and stresses current dominance.
entries.definitionCN: 当前的；主导的；胜诉的。常修饰风、意见或法律当事方，强调当下占优。

entries.definition: intended to stop something from happening. It shares pre- but comes from venire 'to come', not valere.
entries.definitionCN: 预防性的。它共享 pre- 前缀，但来自 venire“来”，并非 valere。

entries.definition: occurring often or shared by many. It is the everyday word, with no trace of 'prevailing force'.
entries.definitionCN: 常见的；共同的。它是日常词，不带“占优势力量”的痕迹。

entries.definition: found over a large area. It stresses geography, while prevalent can stress a group or a period.
entries.definitionCN: 分布广泛的。它强调地理范围，而 prevalent 可强调群体或时期。

entries.definition: most powerful or noticeable. It stresses control, while prevalent stresses how many share something.
entries.definitionCN: 占支配地位的。它强调控制，而 prevalent 强调有多少人共有。

entries.definition: widespread, usually of something bad. It adds a negative judgment that prevalent does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 猖獗的；充斥的。通常指坏事，带有 prevalent 所没有的负面判断。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: The verb prevail means 'to hold sway', so prevalent describes what holds sway across a group.
normal.cn: 动词 prevail 意为“占上风”，所以 prevalent 描述“在一群人中占上风”的东西。

normal.en: prevalent among and prevalent in are the two frames: one for people, one for places.
normal.cn: 与人群连用、与地点连用是两个框架：一个接人群，一个接地点。

normal.en: The noun prevalence supplies the rate; the adjective supplies the description.
normal.cn: 名词 prevalence 提供比率，形容词提供描述。

normal.en: A prevalent wind is simply the wind that blows most often, which shows the scale meaning clearly.
normal.cn: 主导风就是刮得最多的风，清楚显示了“频率占优”的含义。

normal.en: Its natural opposite is rare, and the pair often appears in the same sentence.
normal.cn: 它的天然反义是“罕见”，两者常出现在同一句里。

abstract.en: Picture one style of doorbell on every house along a street.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上每家每户都装同款门铃。

abstract.en: Picture a weather vane that points the same way on most days of the year.
abstract.cn: 想象风向标在一年大多数日子指向同一方向。

abstract.en: Picture a colour that fills most of a mosaic, leaving a few tiles of another shade.
abstract.cn: 想象一种颜色占满马赛克的大部分，只留下几块别的颜色。

examples.en: The practice is prevalent in coastal villages.
examples.cn: 这一做法在沿海村庄很普遍。

examples.en: Malnutrition remains prevalent in the drought zone.
examples.cn: 营养不良在旱区依然普遍。

examples.en: The prevalent assumption turned out to be false.
examples.cn: 那个普遍接受的假设最终被证明是错的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞沃伦特”音近 prevalent：普普通通“沃”得到处都是、连成一“特”——到处都有 → prevalent 普遍的

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前、超过”+ valere“强壮”→ praevalere“占优势”；praevalent- 词干 + -ent 形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all say that something is found in many places or many people, and the differences come from what is being counted.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都说“某物在许多地方或许多人身上出现”，差别在被计数的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one style repeated on every street corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：每个街角都重复着同一种样式。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND CUSTOM: a fear among teachers and an early-marriage custom are both widely copied behaviours.
branches.cn: 人群与习俗：教师的恐惧与早婚习俗都是被广泛模仿的行为。

branches.en: DOMINANCE: a prevailing view and a prevailing wind both hold sway by being the most frequent.
branches.cn: 占优：主导看法与主导风都因最常见而占上风。

branches.en: COUNTED POPULATIONS: disease cases and gene variants are measured by share.
branches.cn: 被计数的人群：病例与基因变体都按占比衡量。

branches.en: LEGAL SPLIT: prevailing keeps the courtroom sense of winning, while prevalent keeps the statistical sense.
branches.cn: 法律分工：prevailing 保留法庭“胜诉”义，prevalent 保留统计义。

branches.en: SCALE: common only means something against rare.
branches.cn: 刻度：常见只有对照罕见才有意义。

intro.en: Prevalent is prae- plus valere plus -ent. The prefix marks superiority, the verb marks strength, and the suffix makes the adjective of a participle.
intro.cn: prevalent 由 prae- 加 valere 加 -ent 构成。前缀标记优势，动词标记力量，后缀把分词构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere 'be strong' → praevalere 'prevail' → praevalens 'prevailing'. English keeps the stem prevalent- and adds no new prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 valere“强壮”→ praevalere“占优势”→ praevalens“占优势的”。英语保留 prevalent- 词干，未加新前缀。

items.example: Reason prevailed in the end.
items.exampleCN: 理智最终占了上风。

items.example: The custom is prevalent in the south.
items.exampleCN: 这一习俗在南方很盛行。

items.example: Prevalence doubled in ten years.
items.exampleCN: 患病率十年间翻倍。

items.example: The prevailing mood was cautious.
items.exampleCN: 主导情绪是谨慎。

items.example: The tone was prevailingly calm.
items.exampleCN: 语气总体上是平静的。

items.example: The claim is valid.
items.exampleCN: 这一主张成立。

items.example: The value of the house rose.
items.exampleCN: 房价上涨了。

items.example: He was praised for valour.
items.exampleCN: 他因英勇受到赞扬。

definition_zh: 促进；便利化；引导；易化
definition_en: the act of making a process easier or helping a group reach its own conclusions without directing them
core_image: 一个人把沉重的门扶住，让后面的人顺利通过
scene: 这里指「促进」。 Trade facilitation cut the time trucks spend waiting at the border.
sceneCN: 这里 facilitation 是「便利化」（第 1 个义项：让流程更顺畅、成本更低）；句意：贸易便利化缩短了卡车在边境等待的时间。图中可辨识物件：边检亭、货车、通关单、时钟。

pos.zh: 促进；便利化；引导；（生理）易化

collocations.zh: 便利费（贿赂的委婉说法）

senses.title: Making a process easier
senses.titleCN: 便利化：让流程少卡几下
senses.definition: the act of removing obstacles so that a process runs more smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 排除障碍、使过程更顺畅的行为
senses.example: The facilitation of visa procedures doubled the number of visiting students.
senses.exampleCN: 签证手续的便利化让来访学生人数翻了一番。
senses.why: facilis means 'easy', from facere 'to do'. Facilitation does not do the work for you; it makes the work easier to do.
senses.whyCN: facilis 意为“容易”，来自 facere“做”。facilitation 不替你做事，而是让事情更容易做。

senses.title: Guiding a group
senses.titleCN: 引导：不替他们决定，只帮他们谈成
senses.definition: the work of helping a group discuss and decide while keeping neutral about the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 帮助群体讨论并作出决定、同时对结果保持中立的工作
senses.example: A trained outsider ran the facilitation of the neighbourhood meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 一位受过训练的外部人员主持了社区会议的引导工作。
senses.why: The facilitator holds the door, not the destination. This modern sense keeps facilis 'easy' but adds the ethical rule of not steering the group.
senses.whyCN: 引导者扶住门，但不决定门通向哪里。这个现代义保留 facilis“容易”，又加上“不操纵群体”的伦理规则。

senses.title: Helping someone learn
senses.titleCN: 助学：把台阶铺到学生脚下
senses.definition: in education, the teacher's support that makes learning possible without doing it for the learner
senses.definitionCN: 教育中教师提供的支持，使学习成为可能，但不代替学习者完成
senses.example: The course trains teachers in the facilitation of small-group discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 该课程训练教师如何引导小组讨论。
senses.why: Learning is the learner's work. Facilitation supplies the easier path: better questions, clearer materials, a safer room.
senses.whyCN: 学习是学习者自己的事。facilitation 提供更容易的路：更好的问题、更清楚的材料、更安全的房间。

senses.title: Physiology: a lowered threshold
senses.titleCN: 易化：让反应更容易被触发
senses.definition: in physiology, the process by which a nerve or reflex response becomes easier to elicit
senses.definitionCN: 生理学上指神经或反射反应变得更容易被引发的过程
senses.example: Repeated stimulation produced facilitation in the spinal pathway.
senses.exampleCN: 反复刺激在脊髓通路中产生了易化。
senses.why: Here 'easy' becomes measurable: the threshold for a response drops. The same Latin word serves a laboratory fact.
senses.whyCN: 这里“容易”变得可测量：反应阈值下降。同一个拉丁词服务于一项实验室事实。

senses.title: Brokering an agreement
senses.titleCN: 促成：把两边的手拉到一起
senses.definition: the act of helping two parties reach an agreement without imposing terms
senses.definitionCN: 帮助两方达成协议而不强加条款的行为
senses.example: His quiet facilitation brought the union and the managers back to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他低调的促成让工会与资方重回谈判桌。
senses.why: The broker removes friction rather than adding force. The word keeps the door-holding image: the parties still walk through it themselves.
senses.whyCN: 中间人减少摩擦，而不是施加力量。这个词保留扶门的意象：门还是当事人自己走过去的。

senses.title: Simplifying paperwork
senses.titleCN: 简化手续：把表格减到最少
senses.definition: the simplification of official procedures and forms
senses.definitionCN: 对官方程序与表格的简化
senses.example: Customs facilitation reduced the number of forms from nine to two.
senses.exampleCN: 海关手续简化把表格从九张减到两张。
senses.why: Administration speaks of facilitation when it removes steps. Each removed form is a door held open.
senses.whyCN: 行政上说 facilitation，指的是去掉步骤。每去掉一张表格，就是扶住一扇门。

senses.title: Trade facilitation
senses.titleCN: 贸易便利化：让货物过境更顺
senses.definition: the specific policy field concerned with lowering the cost of moving goods across borders
senses.definitionCN: 专指降低货物跨境流动成本的政策领域
senses.example: The agreement's trade facilitation chapter covers customs and transit.
senses.exampleCN: 该协定的贸易便利化章节涵盖海关与过境。
senses.why: This is the institutional name for the general sense. WTO documents fixed the phrase, giving 'easy' a permanent policy address.
senses.whyCN: 这是总义项的制度化名称。WTO 文件固定了这个说法，让“容易”有了固定的政策地址。

senses.title: The euphemism for a bribe
senses.titleCN: 便利费：给钱让事情快点办
senses.definition: a payment described as speeding up routine official action, widely treated as a bribe
senses.definitionCN: 被说成加快例行公务的付款，普遍被视为贿赂
senses.example: The audit found facilitation payments recorded as 'express fees'.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现便利费被记作“加急费”。
senses.why: The darker use shows how neutral 'making easy' can be bent: money makes the door open faster, but the door is not yours to open.
senses.whyCN: 这个更黑暗的用法显示中性的“使容易”如何被扭曲：钱让门开得更快，但那扇门不归你开。

intro.en: Facilitation comes from facilitate, from Latin facilitare, built on facilis 'easy'. Facilis itself comes from facere 'to do, make' plus -ilis 'able to be', so 'easy' originally meant 'doable'.
intro.cn: facilitation 来自 facilitate，而 facilitate 出自拉丁 facilitare，建立在 facilis“容易”之上。facilis 本身来自 facere“做、制作”加 -ilis“能被……”，所以“容易”原义是“做得到”。

items.en: facere meant 'to do, make'. It is one of the most productive Latin roots in English: fact, factor, facility, efficient and difficult all trace back to it.
items.cn: facere 意为“做、制作”。它是英语中最能产的拉丁词根之一：fact、factor、facility、efficient、difficult 都能追溯到这里。

items.en: facilis 'easy, doable' joins facere with -ilis 'able to be'. The word describes what can be done without great effort, not what requires no effort.
items.cn: facilis“容易的、做得到的”由 facere 加 -ilis“能被……”构成。它描述不用太大功夫就能做到的事，而不是完全不用功夫的事。

items.en: facilitas meant 'ease, easiness' and also 'ability'. The abstract noun shows that 'easy' and 'capable' were once one idea.
items.cn: facilitas 意为“容易、轻松”，也指“能力”。这个抽象名词显示“容易”与“有能力”曾是同一个观念。

items.en: facilitare 'to make easy' turns the adjective into a verb. The shift from being easy to making easy is the seed of the modern sense.
items.cn: facilitare“使容易”把形容词变成动词。从“容易”到“使容易”，正是现代义的种子。

items.en: English facilitate appears in the 16th century meaning 'to make easy'. The group-process sense, 'to guide without directing', is a 20th-century development.
items.cn: 英语 facilitate 于 16 世纪出现，意为“使容易”。而“引导但不操纵”的群体过程义是 20 世纪的发展。

items.en: Trade facilitation becomes a fixed policy term in the late 20th century, while neural facilitation is an older laboratory usage in physiology.
items.cn: 贸易便利化在 20 世纪末成为固定政策术语，而神经易化是生理学中更早的实验室用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fac- root or the -ilit- shape but splits by suffix; the near-meaning group all involve helping, with different degrees of control.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fac- 词根或 -ilit- 外形，但按后缀分流；近义组都涉及“帮助”，控制程度不同。

entries.definition: to make easier or to guide. It is the action; facilitation is the act or process as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 使容易；引导。它是动作；facilitation 是作为名词的动作或过程。

entries.definition: a place or equipment that makes an activity possible; also ease or aptitude. It names the means, not the helping act.
entries.definitionCN: 使活动成为可能的场所或设备；也指轻松、才能。它命名手段，不是帮助行为。

entries.definition: an expression of congratulations. It looks and sounds close but comes from felix 'happy', not from facilis 'easy'.
entries.definitionCN: 祝贺的话。它形音都接近，但来自 felix“幸福的”，并非 facilis“容易的”。

entries.definition: help with a task. It can involve doing part of the work, while facilitation usually leaves the work with the participants.
entries.definitionCN: 对任务的帮助。它可能包含替做一部分，而 facilitation 通常把工作留给参与者。

entries.definition: the act of giving someone the means or power to do something. It is broader and often technical.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某人做某事的手段或能力。它更宽泛，常带技术色彩。

entries.definition: helping two sides reach agreement by talking between them. It is a specific form of facilitation with a settlement goal.
entries.definitionCN: 在双方之间斡旋以达成协议。它是有“达成和解”目标的特定引导形式。

entries.definition: the act of encouraging or advancing something. It may actively push, while facilitation removes obstacles.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓励或推进某事的行为。它可能主动推动，而 facilitation 是排除障碍。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: facilis 'easy' comes from facere 'do': facilitation makes a thing doable rather than doing it for you.
normal.cn: facilis“容易”来自 facere“做”：facilitation 让事情做得到，而不是替你做。

normal.en: facilitate, facilitator, facility and facilitation share the fac- stem, so one root covers the family.
normal.cn: facilitate、facilitator、facility、facilitation 共享 fac- 词干，一个词根覆盖全家。

normal.en: trade facilitation is the policy name, and group facilitation is the meeting-room name; same door held open.
normal.cn: trade facilitation 是政策名称，group facilitation 是会议室里的名称；都是同一扇被扶住的门。

normal.en: A facilitator is neutral about the outcome, which is what separates facilitation from mediation.
normal.cn: facilitator 对结果保持中立，这正是 facilitation 与 mediation 的分界。

normal.en: Do not confuse felicitation with facilitation: one wishes you happiness, the other makes the work easier.
normal.cn: 别把 felicitation 与 facilitation 混淆：一个祝你好运，一个让工作更容易。

abstract.en: Think of a hand holding a heavy door while someone else walks through.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶住一扇重门，另一个人从门里走过去。

abstract.en: Think of stones removed from a path one by one, until the cart can roll on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象把路上的石头一块块搬走，直到车能自己滚过去。

abstract.en: Think of a guide-rail along a cliff: it does not walk for you, it keeps you from falling.
abstract.cn: 想象悬崖边的护栏：它不替你走路，只让你不掉下去。

examples.en: The facilitation of cross-border payments saved small exporters both time and fees.
examples.cn: 跨境支付的便利化为小出口商节省了时间和费用。

examples.en: Good facilitation leaves the group feeling that the decision was its own.
examples.cn: 好的引导会让小组觉得决定是自己作出的。

examples.en: The study measured neural facilitation after repeated stimulation.
examples.cn: 该研究测量了反复刺激后的神经易化。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扶（facil）你上楼梯”——扶着你、让你更容易走上去 → facilitation 促进、便利化

root: 拉丁 facilis“容易的”（facere“做”+ -ilis“能被……”）→ facilitare“使容易” → facilitate + -ion；核心仍是“让事情做得到”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gesture: a hand holds a door or removes a stone, but the traveller still walks through alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：一只手扶住门或搬走石头，但走路的人仍要自己走过去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding a heavy door open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扶住沉重的门。

branches.en: PROCESS: easing a procedure, simplifying forms and trade facilitation are one removal of steps at three scales.
branches.cn: 流程：便利化程序、简化表格与贸易便利化，是三个尺度上同一种“去掉步骤”。

branches.en: GROUP WORK: guiding a meeting and brokering a deal both hold the space without choosing the outcome.
branches.cn: 群体工作：引导会议与促成协议，都扶住空间却不选择结果。

branches.en: LEARNING: the teacher builds the easier path but does not walk it for the student.
branches.cn: 学习：教师铺出更容易的路，但不替学生走。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY: 'easy' becomes a lowered threshold for a nerve response.
branches.cn: 生理：这里的“容易”变成神经反应阈值的下降。

branches.en: EUPHEMISM: a payment that makes the door open faster shows the same image bent to a bribe.
branches.cn: 委婉语：让门开得更快的付款，把同一意象扭成了贿赂。

intro.en: Facilitation is facilitate plus -ion. The fac- stem means 'do, make', -ilis means 'able to be', -ate makes a verb and -ion names the action.
intro.cn: facilitation 是 facilitate 加 -ion。fac- 词干意为“做、制作”，-ilis 意为“能被……”，-ate 构成动词，-ion 命名动作。

latinIntro.en: The family runs from facere 'do' to facilis 'easy' to facilitas 'ease' to facilitare 'make easy'. English relatives include facility, facilitate, fact and factor.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 facere“做”到 facilis“容易”到 facilitas“轻松”再到 facilitare“使容易”。英语同族词包括 facility、facilitate、fact、factor。

items.meaning: to make easier; to help forward
items.meaningCN: 促进；使便利（-ate 动词后缀）
items.example: The new software facilitates group editing.
items.exampleCN: 新软件方便了多人协同编辑。

items.meaningCN: 促进；便利化（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Facilitation of the talks took two weeks.
items.exampleCN: 会谈的促成工作花了两周。

items.meaning: a person who guides a group neutrally
items.example: The facilitator wrote every idea on the board.
items.exampleCN: 引导者把每个想法都写在白板上。

items.meaning: ease; aptitude; a place or service
items.meaningCN: 容易；才能；设施（-ity 性质名词，来自 facilitas）
items.example: She plays the violin with great facility.
items.exampleCN: 她拉小提琴非常娴熟。

items.meaningCN: 促进的；助长的（-ive 性质形容词）
items.example: The teacher used a facilitative style of questioning.
items.exampleCN: 教师采用了促进式的提问风格。

items.meaning: serving to facilitate, often in physiology
items.meaningCN: 起促进作用的（-ory“用于……”；生理学常用）
items.example: The facilitatory pathway lowers the response threshold.
items.exampleCN: 易化通路降低了反应阈值。

items.meaning: something done or known to be true
items.meaningCN: 事实（facere 的中性过去分词 factum“已做成之事”）
items.example: The fact was checked twice.
items.exampleCN: 这个事实被核对了两遍。

items.meaningCN: 困难的（dis-“不”+ facilis“容易”，与 facilitation 同一词根）
items.example: The final question was the most difficult.
items.exampleCN: 最后一道题是最难的。

definition_zh: 为了……目的；为……之用（后接名词或动名词，说明行为所要达到的目标）
definition_en: in order to achieve a stated aim; for the use or function of something
core_image: 一张便签贴在文件夹上，写明这份材料要办的是哪一件事
scene: 审计员把一摞票据按用途分装，每一袋外面都写着要办的事项。 The clerk sorted the receipts into bags for the purpose of a year-end audit.
sceneCN: 这里取「为了……目的」（第 1 个义项：后接名词短语，点明行为的目标）；句意为职员把票据分袋，为的是年终审计。

pos.zh: 介词短语：为了……目的；为……之用

collocations.phrase: for the purpose of this clause

derivatives.zh: 提议（同拉丁词根，语义已分化）

senses.title: Aim before a noun
senses.titleCN: 目的状语：后接名词说明目标
senses.definition: used before a noun to state the aim that an action is meant to serve
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，说明某一行为所要服务的目标
senses.example: The samples were stored for the purpose of later analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 样品被存放起来，是为了日后分析。
senses.why: Purpose is what is put before the mind, so the phrase takes the aim as a noun rather than as an act.
senses.whyCN: 目的是被放到心前的东西，因此这个短语把目标写成名词，而非写成动作。

senses.title: Aim before a gerund
senses.titleCN: 动名词义：后接动作说明目标
senses.definition: used before a gerund when the aim is itself an activity
senses.definitionCN: 当目标本身是一个活动时，用在动名词前
senses.example: The team met for the purpose of choosing a site.
senses.exampleCN: 团队开会是为了选定一处场地。
senses.why: The gerund names an activity, and the frame keeps it in noun position, where the aim belongs.
senses.whyCN: 动名词指一项活动，而这个框架把它留在名词位置，正是目标该在的位置。

senses.title: The legal formula
senses.titleCN: 法律义：条款中的目的表述
senses.definition: in contracts and statutes it defines why a power is granted or a step is required
senses.definitionCN: 在合同与法规中，用以说明某项权力或某个步骤为何被设定
senses.example: For the purpose of this agreement, the date of delivery is the date of the stamp.
senses.exampleCN: 就本协议而言，交付日期即盖章之日。
senses.why: Legal drafting needs every term pinned down, so the aim of a clause is stated in a fixed frame.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草要求每个词都有确指，因此条款的目的要用固定框架写明。

senses.title: Designed use of a thing
senses.titleCN: 用途义：某物被造来做什么
senses.definition: used before a noun naming the function that an object, room or sum of money is intended to serve
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指出某件物品、某个房间或某笔款项预定的用途
senses.example: This room was built for the purpose of storing grain.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间是为储粮而建的。
senses.why: Here the aim belongs to the object rather than to a person, so purpose slides from intention to function.
senses.whyCN: 这里的目标属于物品而非人，于是目的从意图滑向用途。

senses.title: Why it is not the infinitive frame
senses.titleCN: 语法边界：不能接动词不定式
senses.definition: it takes a noun or a gerund, so a bare infinitive cannot follow it, unlike the shorter purpose markers
senses.definitionCN: 它后接名词或动名词，因此不能接光秃秃的不定式，这与更短的目的标记不同
senses.example: They left early for the purpose of catching the first ferry.
senses.exampleCN: 他们早早出发，是为了赶上头一班渡船。
senses.why: The of in the phrase already governs a nominal element, which is why the verb must be turned into a gerund.
senses.whyCN: 短语中的介词已经支配一个名词性成分，所以动词必须改成动名词。

senses.title: Registration and official use
senses.titleCN: 登记义：官方用途的固定搭配
senses.definition: in registration, taxation and licensing it states the official use that justifies a status
senses.definitionCN: 在登记、税务与许可事务中，说明使某一状态成立的正当事由
senses.example: The vehicle is registered for the purpose of business use.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车是按营业用途登记的。
senses.why: Official categories are uses, not motives, so the same frame labels a status rather than a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 官方分类看的是用途而非动机，因此同一框架标注的是一种身份，而非一种心情。

senses.title: Intention, not result
senses.titleCN: 辨义：说的是意图，不是结果
senses.definition: it states what someone meant to achieve and says nothing about whether it was achieved
senses.definitionCN: 它只说明某人打算达成什么，并不涉及是否真的达成
senses.example: He spoke for the purpose of warning, not of blaming.
senses.exampleCN: 他发言是为了提醒，而不是为了责备。
senses.why: The noun names a projected aim, so a sentence with this phrase can be true even when the aim fails.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指预先设想的目标，因此即使用途落空，句子仍然成立。

senses.title: The formal register
senses.titleCN: 语域义：比口语说法更庄重
senses.definition: in official and academic prose it replaces the plainer shorter purpose markers and sounds more deliberate
senses.definitionCN: 在公文与学术文字中替代更简短的目的说法，语气更审慎
senses.example: The commission was set up for the purpose of reviewing the law.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会之设立，是为了审查这项法律。
senses.why: A longer frame signals deliberateness, which is why statutes and reports favour it over everyday wording.
senses.whyCN: 较长的框架显出审慎，这正是法规与报告偏爱它的原因。

intro.en: Purpose comes from Old French porpos, an intention, from the verb porposer, to put forth, which continues Latin proponere, to place before. The Latin verb is secure; the phrase is modern.
intro.cn: 目的一词来自古法语 porpos「意图」，出自动词 porposer「放到前面」，后者延续拉丁语 proponere「置于前」。拉丁语动词来源清楚；短语属近代。

items.en: Ponere meant to place or set down, and it underlies a large family of English words through its compounds.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、安置，通过其复合形式构成一大批英语词。

items.en: Proponere added the prefix for forward and meant to put something before someone, hence to propose.
items.cn: proponere 加上表向前的前缀，意为把某物摆到人前，由此有提议之义。

items.en: French kept the sense of a plan held in mind, and English borrowed it as purpose.
items.cn: 法语保留了心中所持计划的意思，英语借入后成为目的。

items.en: The noun widened from a person's intention to the function built into an object.
items.cn: 这个名词从人的意图扩展到物品本身被赋予的用途。

items.en: The frame with this preposition and of settles in legal and official drafting; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个介词加 of 的框架在法律与公文中定型，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group looks like a purpose marker but takes a verb or carries another sense; the second group holds genuine purpose frames.
note.cn: 第一组外形接近目的标记，但后接动词或另有他义；第二组才是真正的目的框架。

entries.definition: It takes a verb, so a noun cannot follow it.
entries.definitionCN: 它后接动词，因此不能接名词。

entries.definition: It also takes a verb and usually follows the main clause.
entries.definitionCN: 它同样接动词，通常放在主句之后。

entries.definition: The plural form is the standard variant in contracts.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式是合同中的标准变体。

entries.definition: It describes doing something intentionally, not an aim.
entries.definitionCN: 它指故意去做，而非说明目标。

entries.definition: It introduces a full clause with a modal verb.
entries.definitionCN: 它引出带动情态动词的完整从句。

entries.definition: It takes a noun or gerund and sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 后接名词或动名词，语体正式。

entries.definition: It attaches the aim to the subject as a participle.
entries.definitionCN: 以分词形式把目标挂在主语上。

entries.definition: It states what an object is made to do.
entries.definitionCN: 说明某物被造来做什么。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb for placing before, the legal plural, and the real grammar of noun and gerund.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的拉丁语置前动词、法律复数形式，以及真实的名词与动名词语法。

normal.en: To put something before the mind is to hold it as an aim.
normal.cn: 把某物摆到心前，就是把它当作目标。

normal.en: The noun follows at once, because the aim is treated as a thing.
normal.cn: 名词紧跟其后，因为目标被当作一件东西。

normal.en: An activity must become a gerund before it can stand there.
normal.cn: 活动必须先变动名词，才能放在那个位置。

normal.en: Contracts use the plural variant to cover several aims at once.
normal.cn: 合同用复数变体，以便同时涵盖多个目的。

normal.en: The frame states intention only, never success.
normal.cn: 这个框架只陈述意图，从不保证成功。

abstract.en: Like a label on a box that says what the box is for, not what it contains.
abstract.cn: 像箱外的标签，写明箱子做什么用，而不写里面装了什么。

abstract.en: Like an arrow drawn before the shot: it fixes the target, not the hit.
abstract.cn: 像射击前画下的箭头：定的是靶，不是命中。

abstract.en: Like a clause heading in a contract that tells the reader why the rule exists.
abstract.cn: 像合同里的小标题，告诉读者这条规则为何存在。

examples.en: The survey was conducted for the purpose of testing the new design.
examples.cn: 这项调查是为了检验新设计而进行的。

examples.en: The fund was created for the purpose of helping small farmers.
examples.cn: 该基金是为帮助小农而设立的。

examples.en: Records are kept for the purpose of audit and control.
examples.cn: 保存记录是为了审计与监管。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛 则 破波斯 奥夫」——便签上写明这袋材料要办的事：为了……目的

root: 核心名词意为目的，出自拉丁语 proponere「放到前面」，经古法语 porpos「意图」进入英语；该短语为近代公文定型，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a noun aim to a gerund aim, then to the legal formula, the designed use, the ban on the infinitive, official registration, intention without result, and the formal register.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从名词目标到动名词目标，再到法律条款、物品用途、不能接不定式的语法边界、官方登记、只表意图不表结果，最后是正式语域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note stuck on a folder, stating the one thing this folder is meant to accomplish.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张便签贴在文件夹上，写明这份材料要办的一件事。

branches.en: THE AIM: a noun states the goal that an act is meant to serve.
branches.cn: 目标：名词说明行为所要服务的目标。

branches.en: THE GERUND: an activity is placed in the noun slot, not as an infinitive.
branches.cn: 动名词：活动被放进名词位置，而不是写成不定式。

branches.en: THE USE: rooms and vehicles are labelled by the function they were made for.
branches.cn: 用途：房间与车辆按被造来的用途标注。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: the frame takes no infinitive and claims no result.
branches.cn: 边界：这个框架不接不定式，也不声称结果。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: statutes and reports prefer this fuller, more deliberate wording.
branches.cn: 语域：法规与报告偏爱这种更完整、更审慎的措辞。

intro.en: The phrase is built on a French noun of intention whose Latin base means to place or put.
intro.cn: 这个短语建在一个表意图的法语名词上，其拉丁词根意为放置、安置。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb is ponere, to place, with its prefixed form proponere, to set before; the noun propositum supplied the French sense of intention.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词为 ponere「放置」，其加前缀形式 proponere 意为置于前；名词 propositum 给出法语中的意图义。

items.example: The verb is the base of a whole family of placement words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是一整族表放置词语的根。

items.example: The prefix adds forward movement to placing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀为放置加上向前的方向。

items.example: The noun names what has been put before the mind.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被摆到心前的东西。

items.example: English keeps both the intention and the function.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼指意图与用途。

items.example: The suffix marks the presence of the quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀表示具备这种性质。

items.example: The adverb turns the aim into a manner of acting.
items.exampleCN: 副词把目标转为行动方式。

items.example: The verb keeps the original placing-before image.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留了原本的置前意象。

items.example: The noun names the thing put forward.
items.exampleCN: 名词指被提出的东西。

items.example: The frame is fixed in official prose.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架在公文中已经定型。

definition_zh: 以分析的方式；从分析上；通过对整体的拆解；（数学）解析地（求得精确解）
definition_en: in a manner that uses analysis, by breaking a whole into its parts, or by means of an exact analytical method rather than an approximate one
core_image: 不是绕着整台机器猜，而是把零件逐一摊开、顺着咬合处往下查
scene: 工程师没有画图试凑，而是在纸上解出方程，直接得到曲线的精确交点。 Instead of plotting and guessing, the engineer solves the equation analytically and gets the exact intersection.
sceneCN: 这里 analytically 是「解析地、用精确解法」（第 9 个义项：用解析方法求得闭式精确解，而不是数值近似）；句意：工程师没有画图试凑，而是在纸上解析求解，直接得到精确交点。场景要点：草稿纸上的方程、被划掉的数值表、铅笔写出的根号解、合上的计算器。

pos.zh: 以分析的方式；从分析上；解析地

collocations.zh: 用分析的方法处理问题
解析地求解（求得精确解）
对某事件作分析性考察

derivatives.zh: 分析的；善于分析的；解析的
分析的；解析的（同义变体）

senses.title: In an analytical manner
senses.definition: in a way that uses analysis rather than intuition, habit, or mere description
senses.definitionCN: 以使用分析、而非直觉、习惯或单纯描述的方式
senses.example: The committee examined the proposal analytically, point by point.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会逐点地、以分析的方式审查了这项提案。
senses.why: The -ly suffix turns the adjective into a manner adverb: whatever analytical describes, analytically tells you how it is done. The default sense is simply 'by analysis', with no special field attached.
senses.whyCN: -ly 后缀把形容词变成方式副词：analytical 描述什么，analytically 就说明这件事是怎样做的。默认义项就是“通过分析”，不附带特定领域。

senses.title: By taking the problem apart
senses.definition: by separating a complex problem into smaller parts and dealing with each part in turn
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂问题拆成较小部分，并依次处理每一部分
senses.example: Instead of reacting to the whole crisis, they worked analytically through each cause.
senses.exampleCN: 他们没有对整个危机作出反应，而是分析性地逐一处理每个成因。
senses.why: This makes the core image explicit: the whole is loosened before anything is said about it. The adverb marks the order of work — parts first, whole later — rather than the topic.
senses.whyCN: 这里把核心意象说清楚了：在谈论整体之前，先把它松开。副词标记的是工作的顺序——先部分、后整体——而不是话题。

senses.title: With step-by-step reasoning
senses.definition: by reasoning from premises to conclusion in explicit, checkable steps
senses.definitionCN: 以明确、可核查的步骤从前提到结论进行推理
senses.example: She argued analytically, showing how each claim followed from the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她以分析的方式论证，说明每个论断如何从证据推出。
senses.why: Analysis produces parts, and reasoning links them. When the links are laid out one by one, the manner is analytical in the argumentative sense, close to 'logically' but with the added image of decomposed steps.
senses.whyCN: 分析产生部分，推理连接部分。当这些连接被逐一摆出时，这种方式就是论证意义上的 analytical，接近 logically，但多了一层“步骤被拆开”的意象。

senses.title: By chemical analysis
senses.definition: by means of analytical chemistry, identifying or measuring the components of a sample
senses.definitionCN: 借助分析化学，鉴定或测量样品的组成成分
senses.example: The water was tested analytically for lead and nitrate.
senses.exampleCN: 水样经过分析检测，测定了铅和硝酸盐。
senses.why: In the laboratory the loosening is literal: reagents and instruments separate the sample into measurable components. Analytically here tells you the method used, not the frame of mind.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，松开是字面意义上的：试剂与仪器把样品分离成可测量的成分。这里的 analytically 说明所用方法，而不是心态。

senses.title: From an analytical discipline's perspective
senses.definition: in the manner or perspective of an analytical discipline, such as linguistics or philosophy, rather than a descriptive or historical one
senses.definitionCN: 以分析学科（如语言学或哲学）的方式或视角，而非描述性或历史性视角
senses.example: The novel has been studied analytically by linguists interested in tense.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说被关注时态的语言学家以分析的方式研究过。
senses.why: A discipline trains its members in a method, and the adverb then names the perspective they bring. The same object can be studied historically, descriptively or analytically; the last one asks how its parts are put together.
senses.whyCN: 一个学科用某种方法训练成员，副词随后命名他们带来的视角。同一个对象可以被历史地、描述地或分析地研究；最后一种追问它的各部分如何拼合。

senses.title: Listening in a probing way
senses.titleCN: 以探究、拆解的方式倾听
senses.definition: of a person, in a manner that sorts claims from evidence and tests what is being said
senses.definitionCN: 指人以区分论断与证据、检验对方所说内容的方式
senses.example: He listened analytically, separating what was known from what was assumed.
senses.exampleCN: 他以分析的方式倾听，把已知与假定分开。
senses.why: When the method becomes a personal habit, the adverb describes behaviour rather than procedure. The listener is not cold; he is dividing the speech into claims that can be checked.
senses.whyCN: 当方法变成个人习惯，副词描述的就是行为而非程序。这样的听者并不冷漠；他只是把对方的话分成可核查的论断。

senses.title: In a dissecting written style
senses.definition: of writing or speech, in a style that lays out components and relations instead of narrating or describing
senses.definitionCN: 指写作或言谈以铺陈成分与关系、而非叙述或描写的风格
senses.example: The report describes the policy analytically, with each assumption exposed.
senses.exampleCN: 报告以分析的方式描述这项政策，把每个假设都暴露出来。
senses.why: A style can carry a method. When the sentences are arranged by parts and relations rather than by time or scene, the writing is said to proceed analytically; the adverb modifies the texture of the text.
senses.whyCN: 风格可以承载方法。当句子按部分与关系、而不是按时间或场景排列时，这种写作就被说成以分析的方式展开；副词修饰的是文本的质地。

senses.title: In the manner of analytic philosophy
senses.definition: by the methods of analytic philosophy, clarifying concepts and arguments through logical and linguistic analysis
senses.definitionCN: 以分析哲学的方法，通过逻辑与语言分析澄清概念和论证
senses.example: The question was treated analytically, beginning with the meaning of 'cause'.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题被以分析的方式处理，先从“原因”一词的意义开始。
senses.why: Here the adverb invokes a named tradition. The loosening is applied to concepts: a word is separated into its uses, and a question is answered only after its terms are clarified.
senses.whyCN: 这里的副词唤起一个有名有姓的传统。松开被施于概念：一个词被分成各种用法，问题只有在术语被澄清之后才被回答。

senses.title: By an exact mathematical solution
senses.definition: in mathematics, by obtaining an exact closed-form solution through analysis, as opposed to a numerical approximation
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，通过分析得到闭式精确解，而不是数值近似
senses.example: The equation can be solved analytically, so no iteration is needed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程可以解析求解，因此不需要迭代。
senses.why: In this technical contrast, analysis means deriving the answer from the structure of the equation, not sampling numbers. The adverb marks the route to the result: exact derivation rather than stepwise approximation.
senses.whyCN: 在这一技术性对照里，分析指从方程的结构推出答案，而不是取数值样本。副词标记通往结果的路线：精确推导，而非逐步逼近。

intro.en: Analytically is analytical plus the adverbial suffix -ly. Analytical came into English in the 1520s from Medieval Latin analyticus, from Greek analytikos, whose base analyein means 'to loosen, release' (ana- 'up, back' + lysis 'a loosening'). The adverb therefore says 'in the manner of that loosening'. The suffix -ly is native English, not Greek or Latin: it goes back to Old English -lice and Proto-Germanic *-liko-, cognate with lich 'body' and like.
intro.cn: analytically 是 analytical 加副词后缀 -ly。analytical 于 16 世纪 20 年代从中世纪拉丁语 analyticus 进入英语，再上溯希腊语 analytikos，其词基 analyein 意为“松开、释放”（ana-“向上、向后”加 lysis“松开”）。因此副词说的是“以那种松开的方式”。后缀 -ly 是英语本族成分，不是希腊语或拉丁语：它上溯古英语 -lice 与原始日耳曼语 *-liko-，与 lich“身体”和 like 同源。

items.en: The base adjective analytical is first recorded in English as 'employing analytic methods', via Medieval Latin analyticus from Greek analytikos. The adverb depends on this adjective, so its history begins here.
items.cn: 基础形容词 analytical 最早记录于 16 世纪 20 年代，意为“使用分析方法的”，经中世纪拉丁语 analyticus 来自希腊语 analytikos。副词依附于这个形容词，因此它的历史从这里开始。

items.en: The adverbial -ly comes from Old English -lice, from Proto-Germanic *-liko-, and is cognate with lich 'body' and identical with like (adj.). The modern form emerged in late Middle English, probably under the influence of Old Norse -liga.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 来自古英语 -lice，再上溯原始日耳曼语 *-liko-，与 lich“身体”同源，并与形容词 like 同形。现代形式出现于中古英语晚期，可能受古北欧语 -liga 的影响。

items.en: Analytically is the regular manner adverb from analytical. The etymonline entry for the adverb itself could not be retrieved for this batch because the site returned a bot-check page; the analytical entry lists 'Related: Analytically' but gives no separate date, so the first recorded date of the adverb remains uncertain (unconfirmed here).
items.cn: analytically 是由 analytical 规则构成的方式副词。本批检索时，etymonline 的副词条目因网站返回人机验证页而未能取得；analytical 条目只列出“Related: Analytically”，未给单独年代，因此该副词的首见年代在本批中仍属存疑（未获确认）。

items.en: The adverb spreads with the sciences. Mathematics contrasts solving a problem analytically (exact derivation) with solving it numerically, and analytical chemistry makes 'tested analytically' a laboratory phrase.
items.cn: 这个副词随科学扩展。数学把“解析地求解”（精确推导）与“数值地求解”相对，分析化学则让“以分析方式检测”成为实验室用语。

items.en: Academic English uses analytically for the perspective of a discipline: a text can be read analytically rather than historically or descriptively. Analytic philosophy and analytical psychology supply two named traditions in which the adverb is routine.
items.cn: 学术英语用 analytically 表示某一学科的视角：一部文本可以被分析地阅读，而不是历史地或描述地阅读。分析哲学与分析心理学提供了两个有名有姓的传统，副词在其中是常规用法。

items.en: The adverb is a manner word, not a separate lexical root. It must not be confused with analogically, which comes from analogy and logos 'ratio', or with analytics, a data noun from analysis + -ics. Both look close and neither shares the lysis element.
items.cn: 这个副词是方式词，不是独立的词根。它不能与 analogically 混淆——后者来自 analogy 与 logos“比例”；也不能与 analytics 混淆——后者是 analysis + -ics 的数据名词。两者形近，且都不含 lysis 成分。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective base, its short variant, the data noun analytics and the look-alike analogically; the second compares adverbs that also describe careful thought but do not mean 'by decomposition'.
note.cn: 第一组区分形容词基础、其短变体、数据名词 analytics，以及形似而不同源的 analogically；第二组比较同样描述细致思考、却不含“拆解”之意的副词。

entries.definition: using analysis. It describes a method, mind or account, while analytically describes how an action is performed.
entries.definitionCN: 使用分析的。它描述方法、头脑或论述，而 analytically 描述动作怎样进行。

entries.definition: the shorter form of the same adjective, common in terms such as analytic geometry. It is not the adverb and cannot replace analytically.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较短形式，常见于 analytic geometry 等术语。它不是副词，不能替换 analytically。

entries.definition: the systematic analysis of data. It is a noun from analysis + -ics, not an adverb and not the plural of analytic.
entries.definitionCN: 对数据的系统分析。它是 analysis + -ics 的名词，不是副词，也不是 analytic 的复数。

entries.definition: by analogy, or in a manner based on analogy. It looks almost identical in shape but comes from logos 'ratio', not from lysis 'a loosening'.
entries.definitionCN: 以类比的方式，或基于类比的。它的词形几乎相同，却来自 logos“比例”，而不是 lysis“松开”。

entries.definition: in a way that follows the rules of valid reasoning. Logically stresses the correctness of inference, while analytically stresses the decomposition that supplies the steps.
entries.definitionCN: 以遵循有效推理规则的方式。logically 强调推理的正确性，而 analytically 强调提供这些步骤的拆解。

entries.definition: in an ordered, methodical way that covers everything according to a system. Systematically can be mechanical, while analytically requires taking the subject apart.
entries.definitionCN: 按体系有序、周全地。systematically 可以是机械的，而 analytically 要求把对象拆开。

entries.definition: in a careful, step-by-step manner. Methodically stresses orderly procedure, not the separation of a whole into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 以谨慎、逐步的方式。methodically 强调有序程序，而不强调把整体分成部分。

entries.definition: in a way that examines and judges merits and faults. Critically adds evaluation, while analytically can remain a neutral dissection.
entries.definitionCN: 以审视并评判优缺点的方式。critically 多了一层评价，而 analytically 可以是中性的剖析。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: analytical + -ly, the native English -ly from Old English -lice, and the two look-alikes built on logos and on -ics.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：analytical + -ly、来自古英语 -lice 的本族后缀 -ly，以及两个建立在 logos 和 -ics 上的形似词。

normal.en: analytical + -ly: the suffix changes an adjective into a manner adverb, so analytically means 'in that analytical way'.
normal.cn: analytical + -ly：后缀把形容词变成方式副词，所以 analytically 意为“以那种分析的方式”。

normal.en: -ly is native English, from Old English -lice, cognate with lich 'body' and like. It is not a Greek suffix, even when the base is Greek.
normal.cn: -ly 是英语本族后缀，来自古英语 -lice，与 lich“身体”和 like 同源。即使词基是希腊语，它也不是希腊后缀。

normal.en: The base family: analytical 1520s, analysis 1580s, analyze c.1600. The adverb rides on the adjective.
normal.cn: 基础词族：analytical 是 16 世纪 20 年代，analysis 是 80 年代，analyze 约 1600 年。副词依附于形容词。

normal.en: Mathematics separates 'solve analytically' (exact) from 'solve numerically' (approximate).
normal.cn: 数学把“解析地求解”（精确）与“数值地求解”（近似）分开。

normal.en: analogically is built on logos 'ratio'; analytics is built on -ics. Neither contains lysis 'a loosening'.
normal.cn: analogically 建立在 logos“比例”上；analytics 建立在 -ics 上。两者都不含 lysis“松开”。

abstract.en: Picture a hand loosening a knot: the rope does not disappear, it separates into strands that can be followed one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在松开一个结：绳子没有消失，而是分成可以逐根追踪的股。

abstract.en: The same loosening can be done in thought, in argument, in a lab, in a text or in an equation. The adverb says the action is done that way, not that the topic is analysis.
abstract.cn: 同一种松开可以在思考、论证、实验室、文本或方程中进行。副词说的是动作以这种方式完成，而不是话题属于分析。

abstract.en: In mathematics the manner becomes a choice of route: exact derivation through the structure, instead of walking numerically toward an answer.
abstract.cn: 在数学里，这种方式变成路线选择：顺着结构作精确推导，而不是用数值一步步逼近答案。

examples.en: She prefers to think analytically before making a decision.
examples.cn: 她喜欢在作决定之前先分析性地思考。

examples.en: The two compounds were compared analytically in the same laboratory.
examples.cn: 这两种化合物在同一实验室里经过分析比较。

examples.en: The model can be solved analytically, which makes it useful for teaching.
examples.cn: 这个模型可以解析求解，因此很适合教学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安纳利替扣里」——安纳利把扣子拆开后，一颗一颗地查进去 → analytically 以分析的方式

root: 由形容词 analytical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，字面是“以分析的方式”；analytical 又来自希腊语 analytikos“善于拆解的”，其词基 analyein 意为“松开、拆解”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of analytically, all one manner: something is done by loosening a whole and working through its parts. The field can be a problem, an argument, a lab sample, a discipline, a listener, a text, a philosophical tradition or an equation.
sensesIntro.cn: analytically 的九个义项都来自同一种方式：把整体松开，再顺着各部分去做。领域可以是问题、论证、实验室样品、学科、听者、文本、哲学传统或方程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knot is loosened and its strands are followed one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：把结松开，再一股一股地顺着查下去。

branches.en: GENERAL MANNER: the method itself, the order of taking a problem apart, and the dissecting texture of a text.
branches.cn: 一般方式：方法本身、拆解问题的顺序，以及文本的剖析质地。

branches.en: REASONING AND THE MIND: explicit steps in argument, and a listener who separates claims from evidence.
branches.cn: 推理与头脑：论证中的明确步骤，以及把论断与证据分开的听者。

branches.en: DISCIPLINES: a sample tested in the lab, and a text studied from an analytical perspective.
branches.cn: 学科：实验室里被检测的样品，以及从分析视角被研究的文本。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: concepts are clarified by separating a word into its uses before a question is answered.
branches.cn: 哲学：在回答问题之前，先把一个词分成各种用法以澄清概念。

branches.en: MATHEMATICS: the manner becomes a route, exact derivation instead of numerical approximation.
branches.cn: 数学：方式变成路线，精确推导而非数值近似。

intro.en: Analytically is analytical + -ly, and analytical is analytic + -al. The Greek-Latin core is ana- 'up, back' + lysis 'a loosening'; the English -ly is a native adverbial suffix from Old English -lice. So the word mixes a borrowed Greek base with a native English ending, which is why its form is so regular.
intro.cn: analytically 是 analytical + -ly，而 analytical 是 analytic + -al。希腊—拉丁内核是 ana-“向上、向后”加 lysis“松开”；英语的 -ly 是来自古英语 -lice 的本族副词后缀。因此这个词是 borrowed 的希腊词基加本族英语词尾，这也解释了它为何形式如此规则。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is analyticus (Medieval Latin) and analysis (from Greek). The deepest elements, analyein and lysis, are Greek. There is no separate Latin adverb here: the -ly ending is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 analyticus（中世纪拉丁语）与 analysis（来自希腊语）。最深层的成分 analyein 与 lysis 是希腊语。这里没有独立的拉丁副词：-ly 词尾是英语的。

items.meaningCN: 以分析的方式（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: They reviewed the data analytically.
items.exampleCN: 他们以分析的方式审查了数据。

items.meaningCN: 分析的；使用分析的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: An analytical reading reveals the hidden premise.
items.exampleCN: 分析性的阅读揭示了隐藏的前提。

items.example: Analytic geometry is taught in the first year.
items.exampleCN: 解析几何在第一年讲授。

items.meaning: the breaking up of a whole into parts
items.meaningCN: 把整体分解成部分；分析
items.example: The analysis revealed three separate causes.
items.exampleCN: 分析揭示了三个各自独立的成因。

items.meaning: to break something down to understand it
items.example: The software analyzes the sentence structure.
items.exampleCN: 该软件分析句子结构。

items.example: The analyst wrote a short report.
items.exampleCN: 分析师写了一份简短报告。

items.meaningCN: 数据分析（作为实践或领域）
items.example: Analytics showed a drop in traffic.
items.exampleCN: 数据分析显示流量下降。

items.structure: Old English -lice < Proto-Germanic *-liko-, cognate with lich and like
items.meaning: adverbial suffix meaning 'in the manner of'
items.meaningCN: 副词后缀，意为“以……的方式”（本族英语成分）
items.example: The suffix turns analytical into analytically.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 analytical 变成 analytically。

items.meaning: by analogy; a different root from analytically
items.meaningCN: 以类比的方式（来自 logos，与 analytically 不同源）
items.example: The two cases were treated analogically.
items.exampleCN: 两个案例被以类比的方式处理。

latinEntries.structure: Latin from Greek analysis, ana- + lysis
Greek verb: ana- (up, back) + lyein (to unfasten)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 松开；释放；使自由（希腊语来源）

definition_zh: 生物化学的；与生物体内化学反应有关的
definition_en: relating to the chemical reactions and substances of living organisms
core_image: 细胞内部一张看不见的化学反应网正在运转
scene: 这里指「生物化学的」。 A doctor orders a biochemical test after the patient's liver enzymes rise.
sceneCN: 这里 biochemical 指「生化检验的」（第 3 个义项：用化学反应测定体内物质的检验）；句意：患者肝酶升高后，医生开了一项生化检验。

pos.zh: 生物化学的；生化反应的；生化检验的

derivatives.zh: 从生物化学角度；生化上
生化物质；生化制品（复数）

senses.title: Chemistry inside life
senses.definition: relating to the chemical reactions that take place inside living organisms
senses.definitionCN: 生物化学的；涉及生物体内化学反应的
senses.example: Biochemical reactions in the liver break down most of the alcohol we drink.
senses.exampleCN: 肝脏中的生化反应分解了我们饮用的大部分酒精。
senses.why: bio- names life and chemical names the kind of reaction chemistry studies; joining them yields an adjective for chemistry seen from inside a living body.
senses.whyCN: bio- 指生命，chemical 指化学所研究的那类反应；两者合并，就得到「从生命体内部看化学」的形容词。

senses.title: The substances themselves
senses.definition: concerning the chemical substances that living cells contain or produce
senses.definitionCN: 生物体内化学物质的；涉及活细胞所含或所产生的物质的
senses.example: The study compared biochemical profiles of healthy and diseased tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究比较了健康组织与患病组织的生化成分图谱。
senses.why: Once reactions are named, the molecules they involve also need a label, so the same adjective shifts from the process to the material.
senses.whyCN: 反应被命名之后，参与反应的分子也需要一个说法，于是同一个形容词从「过程」转向「物质」。

senses.title: Laboratory testing
senses.definition: describing a laboratory test that measures chemical substances in blood or other body fluids
senses.definitionCN: 生化检验的；指测定血液等体液中化学物质的实验室检查
senses.example: A routine biochemical screen flagged her elevated liver enzymes.
senses.exampleCN: 一项常规生化筛查发现她的肝酶升高。
senses.why: Hospitals borrowed the adjective for tests that read the body's chemistry, because such a test measures exactly the substances the word already describes.
senses.whyCN: 医院借用这个形容词来指读取体内化学状况的检查，因为这类检查测的正是这个词所描述的物质。

senses.title: Pathways and cycles
senses.definition: relating to a linked series of reactions inside a cell
senses.definitionCN: 生化通路的；指细胞内一串相互衔接的反应
senses.example: Glycolysis is the biochemical pathway that begins the release of energy from glucose.
senses.exampleCN: 糖酵解是启动葡萄糖释能的生化通路。
senses.why: A pathway is a route through the cell's chemical network, so the adjective marks the route rather than any single reaction.
senses.whyCN: 通路是穿越细胞化学网络的一条路线，因此这个形容词标出的是路线，而不是某一个单独的反应。

senses.title: Oxygen demand in water
senses.definition: in environmental science, describing the oxygen that microbes consume while decomposing organic matter in water
senses.definitionCN: 生化需氧量的；环境科学中指微生物分解水中有机物时所耗的氧
senses.example: The biochemical oxygen demand of the effluent was twice the permitted level.
senses.exampleCN: 该废水的生化需氧量是允许水平的两倍。
senses.why: The standard test lets living microbes do the chemical work, so the adjective records that a biological agent carries out the oxidation being measured.
senses.whyCN: 这项标准检测让活的微生物去完成化学工作，因此这个形容词说明：被测量的氧化过程是由生物主体完成的。

senses.title: Markers and signatures
senses.definition: describing a molecule whose level signals a disease or a biological state
senses.definitionCN: 生化标志物的；指含量可提示疾病或生理状态的分子
senses.example: A biochemical marker in the blood can reveal heart muscle damage.
senses.exampleCN: 血液中的一种生化标志物可以提示心肌损伤。
senses.why: A marker is a substance that stands for a hidden condition, and the adjective says the signal is chemical and arises from a living process.
senses.whyCN: 标志物是用一种物质代表看不见的状况，而这个形容词说明信号是化学的、来自生命过程。

senses.title: Weapons and agents
senses.definition: relating to weapons that use chemicals or living organisms to cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 生化战剂的；指用化学物质或活生物造成伤害的武器
senses.example: International law prohibits the development of biochemical weapons.
senses.exampleCN: 国际法禁止研发生化武器。
senses.why: The compound was extended from laboratory chemistry to the chemistry of life turned into a weapon, keeping both halves of the word literal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从实验室化学延伸到「被武器化的生命化学」，两个字面成分都保持了原义。

senses.title: Molecular explanations
senses.definition: explaining a biological effect by the underlying chemistry
senses.definitionCN: 以生化机制解释的；用底层化学反应说明生物现象
senses.example: The team gave a biochemical explanation for how the bacterium resists the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 该团队从生化机制上解释了这种细菌为何能抵抗该药物。
senses.why: When an effect is explained by reactions and molecules rather than by anatomy, the adjective labels the level of explanation rather than the thing explained.
senses.whyCN: 当一个效应是用反应和分子、而不是用解剖结构来解释时，这个形容词标出的是解释的层次，而不是被解释的对象。

intro.en: Biochemical joins a Greek prefix for life to a word whose own origin is disputed, then adds a Latin adjective ending.
intro.cn: biochemical 把一个表示「生命」的希腊语前缀，接在一个本身来源尚有争议的词上，再加拉丁语形容词词尾。

items.en: The prefix bio- comes from Greek bios, 'life, course of life'. Scientific Latin made it a productive prefix in the late 18th and 19th centuries.
items.cn: 前缀 bio- 出自希腊语 bios「生命、生命历程」。科学拉丁语在 18 世纪末至 19 世纪把它变成了能产的构词成分。

items.en: Chemical goes back through alchemy to Medieval Latin alchimia and Arabic al-kimiya, usually traced to Greek khemeia, the art of working metals. The further origin is disputed, sometimes linked to an Egyptian place name; this part is uncertain.
items.cn: chemical 经 alchemy 上溯至中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 与阿拉伯语 al-kimiya，通常追溯到希腊语 khemeia「冶金术」。更早的来源有争议，有时被联系到埃及地名；这一层属于来源不确定。

items.en: The compound biochemical appears in scientific writing in the first half of the 19th century, when biology and chemistry were separating into distinct disciplines. The exact first use is not firmly established.
items.cn: biochemical 这一复合词一般认为出现在 19 世纪上半叶的科学写作中，当时生物学与化学正分化为独立学科。确切的首见出处尚未定论。

items.en: In the 20th century the adjective became routine in hospitals, where a biochemical test means a panel of measurements on blood or urine.
items.cn: 进入 20 世纪，这个形容词在医院里成为常规用法，biochemical test 指对血液或尿液进行的一组测定。

items.en: The phrase biochemical oxygen demand was standardized in the early 20th century for measuring organic pollution in water.
items.cn: biochemical oxygen demand 这一说法在 20 世纪初被标准化，用于衡量水中的有机污染。

items.en: From the mid-20th century, biochemical was also attached to weapons and agents, broadening the word beyond the laboratory.
items.cn: 自 20 世纪中叶起，biochemical 又被用于武器与战剂，使这个词越出实验室的范围。

note.en: The first group holds look-alike words built on the same or neighbouring elements; the second holds words that overlap in meaning but differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同用相近构词成分、容易看混的词；第二组是词义相交但范围不同的词。

entries.definition: Relating to living things or to the science of life. It is broader than biochemical because it does not commit to chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 指与生物或生命科学有关的，范围比 biochemical 宽，因为它不限定在化学层面。

entries.definition: Names the discipline or the chemical processes themselves; biochemical is the form that modifies nouns such as test, pathway or weapon.
entries.definitionCN: 是名词，指学科或化学过程本身；修饰 test、pathway、weapon 等名词时要用 biochemical。

entries.definition: Names the chemical substances themselves, especially industrial products; the adjective biochemical has no plural.
entries.definitionCN: 是复数名词，指化学物质本身，尤指工业制品；形容词 biochemical 没有复数形式。

entries.definition: Relating to metabolism, the sum of chemical changes in a body. It overlaps with biochemical but is tied specifically to metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 指与新陈代谢有关的，即体内化学变化的总和；与 biochemical 有交集，但专指代谢。

entries.definition: Relating to the normal functions of organs and tissues, including but not limited to their chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 指器官与组织的正常功能，包含化学层面但并不限于化学层面。

entries.definition: Relating to molecules as such, in any context; biochemical adds that the molecules belong to living systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指分子层面本身，可用于任何领域；biochemical 则补充说明这些分子属于生命系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + chemical: chemistry as it happens inside a living body.
normal.cn: bio-「生命」+ chemical「化学」：发生在活体内部的化学。

normal.en: The family runs biochemistry, biochemist, biochemicals and biochemically.
normal.cn: 同族词有 biochemistry、biochemist、biochemicals、biochemically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: biochemical test, biochemical pathway, biochemical marker, biochemical oxygen demand.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义项：生化检验、生化通路、生化标志物、生化需氧量。

normal.en: Hospitals use a biochemical panel the way a mechanic uses a diagnostic scan.
normal.cn: 医院用生化检查组套，就像修理工用诊断扫描。

normal.en: The word keeps both halves visible: life on the left, chemistry on the right.
normal.cn: 这个词把两半都摆在明面上：左边是生命，右边是化学。

abstract.en: Think of a factory floor: the machines are chemical reactions, and the whole floor is alive.
abstract.cn: 想象一间车间：机器是化学反应，而整个车间是活的。

abstract.en: A biochemical marker is a smoke alarm for the body: it does not cause the fire, it reports it.
abstract.cn: 生化标志物像身体的烟雾报警器：它不制造火，只报告火。

abstract.en: Picture a river and a sewage plant: the microbes are workers, and their oxygen use is the bill they leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河与一座污水厂：微生物是工人，它们耗掉的氧就是留下的账单。

examples.en: Biochemical reactions in the liver break down most of the alcohol we drink.
examples.cn: 肝脏中的生化反应分解了我们饮用的大部分酒精。

examples.en: A biochemical test can detect damage before an imaging scan shows it.
examples.cn: 生化检验可以在影像扫描显示之前发现损伤。

examples.en: The researchers traced the insect's resistance to a biochemical change in its nerve cells.
examples.cn: 研究者把这种昆虫的抗药性追溯到其神经细胞中的一处生化改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bio（生命）+ chemical（化学）」→ 生命里的化学 → 生物化学的、生化检验的

root: 希腊语 bios「生命」+ 希腊语 khemeia「冶金术」（经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 与中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 进入英语）→ chemical；再加形容词后缀 -al 构成 biochemical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: chemistry happening inside life. The same adjective then moves from reactions to substances, to tests, to pathways, to markers, and finally to weapons and to explanations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个想法展开：化学在生命内部发生。同一个形容词从反应移向物质，再移向检验、通路、标志物，最后延伸到武器与解释方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible web of reactions turning matter inside a living cell.
core.cn: 核心意象：活细胞内部一张看不见的反应网在转化物质。

branches.en: THE CORE: chemistry viewed inside a living body, whether as the subject of study or as the level of explanation.
branches.cn: 核心：从活体内部看化学，既可以是被研究的对象，也可以是解释的层次。

branches.en: MATTER AND MEASUREMENT: the molecules involved, and the laboratory tests that read them.
branches.cn: 物质与测量：参与其中的分子，以及读取这些分子的实验室检验。

branches.en: THE ROUTE: a pathway is the order in which the reactions run.
branches.cn: 路线：通路就是这些反应运行的先后顺序。

branches.en: THE ENVIRONMENT: microbes doing the chemistry become a standard measure of water quality.
branches.cn: 环境：由微生物完成的化学过程成为水质的标准量度。

branches.en: SIGNAL AND THREAT: the same chemistry can report disease or be turned into a weapon.
branches.cn: 信号与威胁：同一套化学既能报告疾病，也能被做成武器。

intro.en: The word is a transparent compound: a Greek prefix for life, an English word for chemistry, and a Latin adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词的构造透明：一个表示生命的希腊语前缀，一个表示化学的英语词，以及一个拉丁语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The first element is Greek; the second reached English through Arabic and Medieval Latin. The Latin adjective ending -alis supplies -al.
latinIntro.cn: 第一个成分来自希腊语；第二个成分经阿拉伯语与中世纪拉丁语进入英语；形容词词尾 -al 来自拉丁语 -alis。

items.meaning: relating to the chemistry of living things
items.example: The biochemical pathway was mapped step by step.
items.exampleCN: 这条生化通路被逐步绘出。

items.meaning: the science of the chemistry of life
items.example: She teaches biochemistry to medical students.
items.exampleCN: 她给医学生讲授生物化学。

items.meaning: a person who studies the chemistry of life
items.example: The biochemist purified the enzyme from liver tissue.
items.exampleCN: 这位生物化学家从肝组织中纯化了该酶。

items.meaning: relating to living things or to biology
items.meaningCN: 与生物或生物学有关的
items.example: The lake supports a rich biological community.
items.exampleCN: 这座湖养育着丰富的生物群落。

items.example: Molecular biology grew out of biochemistry.
items.exampleCN: 分子生物学是从生物化学中发展出来的。

items.meaning: a substance that works against bacteria
items.example: The doctor prescribed a course of antibiotics.
items.exampleCN: 医生开了一个疗程的抗生素。

items.meaning: relating to chemistry or to substances used in it
items.meaningCN: 与化学或化学物质有关的
items.example: The factory stores chemical waste in sealed tanks.
items.exampleCN: 工厂把化学废料存放在密封罐中。

items.example: The chemist tested the purity of the sample.
items.exampleCN: 化学家检测了样本的纯度。

items.meaning: the medieval art of transforming metals
items.meaningCN: 中世纪转化金属的技艺
items.example: Alchemy preceded modern chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 炼金术先于现代化学出现。

items.meaning: in terms of the chemistry of life
items.example: The two tissues are biochemically distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这两种组织在生化上是有区别的。

latinEntries.meaning: metalworking; the art later called chemistry
latinEntries.meaningCN: 冶金术；后来称为化学的技艺

definition_zh: 政治学家；以政治学为专业的研究者、教师或分析者
definition_en: a person who studies government and political behaviour professionally, whether as a researcher, teacher, author or analyst
core_image: 选举夜的研究室里，几个人盯着屏幕上的选区数据，把出口民调逐项填进模型
scene: 选举夜的研究室里，几个人盯着屏幕上的选区数据，把出口民调逐项填进模型。 The political scientist warned that the model missed turnout in rural districts.
sceneCN: 这里指「以数据模型研究选举的政治学者」，对应第 6 个义项：用统计手段预测选举结果的研究者；句意为这位政治学家警告说，模型漏掉了乡村选区的投票率。画面要点：夜间研究室、选区数据屏、手写记录。

pos.zh: 政治学家；政治学研究者（可指学者、教师、撰稿人或分析者）

collocations.zh: 研究投票率问题的政治学家

derivatives.zh: 唯科学主义（把科学方法滥用到一切领域的倾向）

senses.title: A professional researcher of politics
senses.titleCN: 以研究政治为专业的人
senses.definition: a person whose job is to study how authority is won, used and limited, and to publish the results
senses.definitionCN: 以研究权威如何被赢得、使用与限制并发表成果为职业的人
senses.example: The political scientist spent four years counting committee votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这位政治学家花了四年时间清点委员会表决。
senses.why: the compound simply puts the practitioner suffix on the name of the field, so the person is defined by what he studies.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词只是把表人后缀加在学科名上，因此此人是按他研究什么来定义的。

senses.title: A university teacher of the subject
senses.titleCN: 在大学讲授这一学科的人
senses.definition: a lecturer or professor whose working life is divided between teaching and research
senses.definitionCN: 工作分为教学与研究两部分的讲师或教授
senses.example: A political scientist taught the introductory course to two hundred students.
senses.exampleCN: 一位政治学家给两百名学生上入门课。
senses.why: the same title covers research and teaching because universities joined the two in one post.
senses.whyCN: 同一个称谓同时涵盖研究与教学，因为大学把这两件事并入了同一个职位。

senses.title: The author of studies and textbooks
senses.titleCN: 撰写论著与教科书的人
senses.definition: a person known through written work rather than through a post, cited by others in the field
senses.definitionCN: 以著作而非职位为人所知、并被同行引用的人
senses.example: The textbook was written by a political scientist who had never held office.
senses.exampleCN: 这本教科书出自一位从未担任公职的政治学家之手。
senses.why: a discipline circulates through text, so authorship becomes a way of being a political scientist.
senses.whyCN: 学科靠文本流通，因此写作本身也成了一种做政治学家的方式。

senses.title: An analyst who comments on current events
senses.titleCN: 就时局发表评论的分析者
senses.definition: a person with academic training who explains elections, coups or coalitions to a general audience
senses.definitionCN: 受过学术训练、向普通受众解释选举、政变或联合政府的人
senses.example: The paper hired a political scientist to explain the coalition talks.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸请了一位政治学家来解释联合组阁谈判。
senses.why: expertise becomes public when the press needs a quick explanation, and the academic title travels with it.
senses.whyCN: 当媒体需要快速解释时，专业知识就进入公共视野，学术头衔也随之而来。

senses.title: A specialist in one country or one institution
senses.titleCN: 某一国家或某一机构的研究专家
senses.definition: a researcher whose authority rests on deep knowledge of a particular political system
senses.definitionCN: 权威建立在对某一具体政治制度的深入了解之上的研究者
senses.example: A political scientist of the region predicted the split years early.
senses.exampleCN: 一位研究该地区的政治学家多年前就预言了那次分裂。
senses.why: the field divides by area, so the title is often completed by the name of a country or a chamber.
senses.whyCN: 这一领域按地区分工，因此这个称谓后面常接上一个国家或一个议院的名字。

senses.title: A modeler or forecaster of elections
senses.definition: a person who builds statistical models of voting and publishes probability estimates
senses.definitionCN: 构建投票统计模型并发布概率估计的人
senses.example: The political scientist warned that the model missed rural turnout.
senses.exampleCN: 这位政治学家警告说，模型漏掉了乡村投票率。
senses.why: the empirical promise inside the field's name is most visible when its results are numbers that can be checked.
senses.whyCN: 当研究结果是可核对的数字时，学科名称里那项实证承诺最为明显。

senses.title: An adviser to governments or parties
senses.titleCN: 为政府或政党提供建议的人
senses.definition: a researcher who applies findings inside an administration, campaign or international body
senses.definitionCN: 把研究成果用在政府、竞选团队或国际机构内部的研究者
senses.example: The political scientist briefed the cabinet on referendum risks.
senses.exampleCN: 这位政治学家就公投风险向内阁作了简报。
senses.why: knowledge about power can be sold to those who hold it, so the title also appears inside the state.
senses.whyCN: 关于权力的知识可以卖给掌握权力的人，因此这个称谓也会出现在国家机构内部。

senses.title: Abstract: one who makes power legible
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：让权力变得可读的人
senses.definition: in general use, anyone who renders the workings of authority visible and comparable
senses.definitionCN: 泛指把权威的运作方式变得可见、可比较的人
senses.example: In a faction fight, the political scientist is the one drawing the map.
senses.exampleCN: 在派系争斗中，政治学家就是那个画地图的人。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the task of description, and the university setting falls away.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留描述这项任务，大学场景则被去掉。

intro.en: Political scientist is an English compound of the field's name, itself a nineteenth-century pairing of a Greek civic adjective with a Latin noun for knowledge. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: political scientist 是由学科名构成的英语复合词，而学科名本身是十九世纪把希腊的城邦形容词与拉丁的知识名词配成的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polis meant a city-state and its citizen body; its deeper origin is not established, and the pre-Greek suggestion remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: polis 指城邦及其公民总体；它更深的来源未得到证明，前希腊语来源的说法仍属假说。

items.en: Scientia meant 'knowledge', from scire 'to know'; the further origin of scire is uncertain and the link sometimes drawn to scindere 'to split' is not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: scientia 意为「知识」，出自 scire「知道」；scire 的更早来源不确定，有人把它与 scindere「切开」相联系，但并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Science entered English in the fourteenth century meaning knowledge or skill in general, and only in the nineteenth century did it come to mean the natural sciences in particular.
items.cn: science 在十四世纪进入英语，泛指知识或技艺，直到十九世纪才专指自然科学。

items.en: The word scientist is generally attributed to William Whewell, who proposed it in 1834 to match artist; before that, those who studied nature were called natural philosophers.
items.cn: scientist 一词一般认为是威廉·休厄尔在 1834 年为与 artist 对应而提出的；在此之前，研究自然的人被称为自然哲学家。

items.en: Political scientist appeared as the discipline acquired chairs and journals in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, modelled on the older titles of natural science.
items.cn: 随着这门学科在十九世纪末、二十世纪初设立教席与期刊，political scientist 这一称谓按自然科学既有的头衔模式出现。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same parts that are easily confused with the person; group two holds neighbouring professions that also explain politics.
note.cn: 第一组是用同样构件构成、容易与这个表人名词混淆的词；第二组是同样解释政治现象的邻近职业。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; the person holds a post or a degree in it, but the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科本身；此人可能在其中任职或取得学位，但两者不能互换。

entries.definition: By itself the word usually means a natural scientist; the qualifier is what points to the social field.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时通常指自然科学家；正是前面的限定语才把它指向社会领域。

entries.definition: A person who holds or seeks office; a political scientist studies such people and may never run for anything.
entries.definitionCN: 担任或谋求公职的人；政治学家研究这类人，自己可能从不参选。

entries.definition: An adjective describing method; it can modify political science but does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述方法的形容词；可修饰政治学，但不能指人。

entries.definition: A specialist in the study of voting and election statistics; the focus is narrower than the whole discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 专门研究投票与选举统计的人；范围比整个学科窄。

entries.definition: A person who conducts opinion surveys, often commercially; a political scientist may use polls without being one.
entries.definitionCN: 从事民意调查的人，常为商业机构工作；政治学家可能使用民调，但本身未必是民调从业者。

entries.definition: A person who evaluates specific programmes and advises on choices; the work is applied rather than academic.
entries.definitionCN: 评估具体方案并就选择提出建议的人；工作偏应用而非学术。

entries.definition: A person who explains events to an audience; training may be in journalism or law rather than in political science.
entries.definitionCN: 向受众解释时事的人；其训练可能来自新闻或法律，而非政治学。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The field name plus the practitioner suffix: a person defined by the subject studied.
normal.cn: 学科名加表人后缀：按所研究的学科来定义的人。

normal.en: The first half is a Greek civic adjective, the second half rests on a Latin verb meaning to know.
normal.cn: 前半是希腊的城邦形容词，后半立在拉丁语中表示「知道」的动词上。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the roles: a leading political scientist, a political scientist by training.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示各种角色：一流政治学家、出身政治学专业的人。

normal.en: The near pair to keep apart is politician, who practices, and political scientist, who studies.
normal.cn: 要分清的一对近邻是实践政治的从政者与研究政治的政治学家。

normal.en: Many political scientists never hold office, and many officeholders never study the subject.
normal.cn: 许多政治学家从不担任公职，许多公职人员也从不研究这门学科。

abstract.en: Picture a person drawing a map of a building they have never entered.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人画着一栋自己从未进去过的建筑的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a night desk where numbers from distant districts arrive one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张夜班桌，远处各区的数字一个接一个送来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at a chart and saying: this is how the decision was actually made.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手点着图表说：决定实际上是这样作出的。

examples.en: Political scientists have argued for decades about turnout.
examples.cn: 政治学家就投票率问题争论了几十年。

examples.en: A political scientist by training, she now runs an election unit.
examples.cn: 她出身政治学专业，现在主持一个选举研究部门。

examples.en: The commission included two political scientists and one judge.
examples.cn: 该委员会包括两位政治学家和一位法官。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「政治学 + 人」——把谁说了算当成专业来研究的人 → 政治学家

root: political 出自希腊 politikos「公民的、城邦的」，源头 polis「城邦」；scientist 由拉丁 scientia「知识」加表人后缀构成，该词一般认为是 1834 年由休厄尔提出。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one qualification: a person certified to study power can be a researcher, a teacher, an author, a commentator, an area specialist, a forecaster, an adviser, and finally anyone who makes authority visible.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种资格展开：被认定有资格研究权力的人，可以是研究者、教师、著者、评论者、地区专家、预测者、顾问，最后是任何让权威变得可见的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a night desk where district numbers are entered into a model.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张夜班桌，各区的数字被逐项输进模型。

branches.en: RESEARCH: the base sense, a person whose trade is producing knowledge about authority.
branches.cn: 研究：基础义，即以生产关于权威的知识为业的人。

branches.en: TEACH AND WRITE: the same knowledge is handed on in a lecture hall or fixed on a page.
branches.cn: 教与写：同一套知识，或在讲堂里传给他人，或在纸页上固定下来。

branches.en: PUBLIC AND DEEP: the general explainer and the country specialist are two ways of being useful.
branches.cn: 通俗与专深：面向大众的解释者与钻研一国的专家，是两种有用的方式。

branches.en: PREDICT AND ADVISE: numbers are produced ahead of events and then handed to those who decide.
branches.cn: 预测与建议：数字在事件之前造出，随后交到作决定的人手里。

branches.en: LEGIBILITY: strip the institution away and the task is to make power readable.
branches.cn: 可读性：把机构抽走，剩下的任务就是让权力变得可读。

intro.en: The compound stacks two learned words, each with its own suffix, so the title can be read from the end backwards.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把两个学术词叠在一起，各带自己的后缀，因此这个称谓可以从末尾往前读。

latinIntro.en: Latin scientia and scire supply science, scientific and scientist; politicus supplies the civic qualifier.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 scientia 与 scire 提供科学、科学的与科学家；politicus 提供城邦这一限定语。

items.example: The qualifier starts from the city.
items.exampleCN: 这个限定语从城邦开始。

items.example: The adjective names the object of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指出研究对象。

items.example: The base verb carries the claim to knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载对知识的主张。

items.example: The noun names what the person is supposed to produce.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指出此人应当生产的东西。

items.example: The suffix marks the practitioner.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记从业者。

items.example: The word was proposed in the eighteen thirties.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是在十九世纪三十年代提出的。

items.example: The field gave the title its first half.
items.exampleCN: 这一学科给这个称谓提供了前半部分。

items.example: A scientific claim can be tested.
items.exampleCN: 科学的论断可以被检验。

items.example: Scientism applies the method where it does not fit.
items.exampleCN: 唯科学主义把方法用在并不适合的地方。
