latinEntries.exampleCN: nauticus 把希腊语 nautes 带入拉丁语。

definition_zh: 核糖体；由 rRNA 与蛋白质组成、在细胞内合成蛋白质的颗粒状细胞器
definition_en: a particle made of ribosomal RNA and proteins on which messenger RNA is translated into protein
core_image: 上下两片不规则的大块夹住一条细长的带子，带子从两片之间穿过，旁边不断掉下小珠子串成链
scene: 这里指「核糖体」。 A ribosome reads the message in mRNA and joins amino acids into a chain.
sceneCN: 这里 ribosome 指「核糖体」这一细胞器整体（第 1 个义项：由 rRNA 与蛋白组成、进行翻译的颗粒）；它读取 mRNA 上的信息并把氨基酸连成链。图中可辨识物件：大亚基、小亚基、穿过的 mRNA 带、串起的氨基酸链。

pos.zh: 核糖体（可数，复数 ribosomes）

derivatives.zh: 核酶（具催化活性的 RNA）

senses.title: The particle that makes protein
senses.titleCN: 核糖体：合成蛋白质的颗粒
senses.definition: the RNA-protein particle in a cell on which proteins are assembled
senses.definitionCN: 细胞内由 RNA 与蛋白质组成、组装蛋白质的颗粒
senses.example: Every cell needs thousands of ribosomes to keep up with protein demand.
senses.exampleCN: 每个细胞都需要成千上万个核糖体才能满足蛋白质需求。
senses.why: ribo- points to ribonucleic acid and -some to a body, so the coined word names a body made of RNA.
senses.whyCN: ribo- 指向核糖核酸，-some 指向「体」，因此这个新造词命名一个由 RNA 构成的「体」。

senses.title: Two kinds of material in one particle
senses.definition: the composition of the particle, roughly two thirds RNA and one third protein in bacteria
senses.definitionCN: 该颗粒的组成，在细菌中约三分之二为 RNA、三分之一为蛋白质
senses.example: Ribosomal RNA forms the core that holds the proteins in place.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体 RNA 构成核心，把蛋白质固定在位。
senses.why: the particle was first seen as a granule and only later shown to be a mixture, so the name covers its material as well.
senses.whyCN: 该颗粒起初只被当作一种颗粒，后来才被证明是混合物，于是这个名字也覆盖了它的材料。

senses.title: The act of translation
senses.definition: the particle's function of translating a messenger RNA sequence into an amino acid chain
senses.definitionCN: 把信使 RNA 的序列翻译成氨基酸链的功能
senses.example: On the ribosome, codons are matched to transfer RNAs one by one.
senses.exampleCN: 在核糖体上，密码子被逐个与转运 RNA 配对。
senses.why: because the particle reads one code and writes another, its name is used for the act of translation itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为这颗粒读一种编码、写另一种编码，它的名字也被用于翻译这个动作本身。

senses.title: A large and a small subunit
senses.definition: the two-subunit architecture, a small subunit that binds messenger RNA and a large subunit that forms the exit tunnel
senses.definitionCN: 双亚基构造：小亚基结合信使 RNA，大亚基形成出口通道
senses.example: The small ribosomal subunit selects the start codon.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体小亚基负责选择起始密码子。
senses.why: electron microscopy resolved one particle into two unequal halves, so the word also names that division.
senses.whyCN: 电镜把一个颗粒解析为大小不等的两半，于是这个词也指这种分法。

senses.title: Many at once on one message
senses.titleCN: 多聚核糖体：一条信使上串多个颗粒
senses.definition: a group of ribosomes translating the same message simultaneously, forming a polysome
senses.definitionCN: 多个核糖体同时翻译同一条信使而形成的多聚核糖体
senses.example: Polysomes let a cell produce many copies of one protein quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 多聚核糖体让细胞迅速产生同一蛋白的许多拷贝。
senses.why: when several particles were seen spaced along one thread, the singular name was extended to the collective.
senses.whyCN: 当人们看到多个颗粒沿一条细线排开，单数名称便扩展到这个集合。

senses.title: The docking site on a message
senses.titleCN: 结合位点：信使上的停靠处
senses.definition: the sequence in a messenger RNA where the ribosome attaches and starts translation
senses.definitionCN: 信使 RNA 上核糖体附着并开始翻译的序列
senses.example: A strong ribosome binding site raises the yield of the encoded protein.
senses.exampleCN: 强核糖体结合位点会提高所编码蛋白的产量。
senses.why: the particle must stand somewhere before it works, so its name attaches to the landing pad as well.
senses.whyCN: 这颗粒工作之前必须站到某处，于是它的名字也附着在「停机坪」上。

senses.title: A target for antibiotics
senses.titleCN: 药物靶点：抗生素作用的部位
senses.definition: the particle regarded as a drug target, because bacterial and human ribosomes differ enough to be told apart
senses.definitionCN: 把该颗粒视为药物靶点，因为细菌与人的核糖体差异足以区分
senses.example: Streptomycin binds the bacterial ribosome and blocks its proofreading.
senses.exampleCN: 链霉素结合细菌核糖体并阻断其校对。
senses.why: since the particle differs between kingdoms, medicine reads it as a place where one kind can be hit without the other.
senses.whyCN: 由于该颗粒在不同界之间互有差异，医学把它读成「可打击一类而不伤另一类」的位置。

senses.title: The conserved core of translation
senses.titleCN: 进化保守性：翻译机制的共同核心
senses.definition: the particle as a deeply conserved structure shared by all living cells, with bacterial 70S and eukaryotic 80S versions
senses.definitionCN: 该颗粒作为所有活细胞共有的高度保守结构，细菌为 70S、真核为 80S
senses.example: The ribosome's catalytic core is RNA, a trace of the RNA world.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体的催化核心是 RNA，这是 RNA 世界的一条痕迹。
senses.why: its shape is so similar across species that the particle is read as a fossil of early life, not just a machine.
senses.whyCN: 它在各物种间形状极为相似，因此被读成早期生命的化石，而不只是一台机器。

intro.en: Ribosome is a twentieth-century coinage from ribo-, short for ribonucleic acid, plus -some from Greek soma 'body'. It has no classical Latin ancestry.
intro.cn: ribosome 是 20 世纪的合成词：ribo- 是 ribonucleic acid 的缩略，-some 来自希腊 soma「身体」。它没有古典拉丁语源。

items.en: Greek soma meant 'body'. The scientific suffix -some had already been used for cell bodies and particles before ribosome appeared.
items.cn: 希腊 soma 意为「身体」。在 ribosome 出现之前，科学后缀 -some 已用于指细胞体和颗粒。

items.en: ribo- is a shortening of ribonucleic acid, named from ribose, the sugar first identified in the 1890s.
items.cn: ribo- 是 ribonucleic acid 的缩略，后者由 ribose 得名，这种糖于 1890 年代被鉴定。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and coiner): the word is generally credited to Richard B. Roberts around 1958, but the exact date and occasion are not firmly documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与首创者）：一般认为由 Richard B. Roberts 于 1958 年前后提出，但确切年代与场合并无坚实文献记录。

items.en: Electron microscopy in the mid-1950s showed dense granules on the endoplasmic reticulum, and the name was applied to them.
items.cn: 20 世纪 50 年代中期的电镜显示内质网上有致密颗粒，该名称被用在这些颗粒上。

items.en: In the 1960s and 1970s the particle was resolved into subunits and its RNA core was shown to be catalytic, fixing the modern senses.
items.cn: 20 世纪 60 至 70 年代，该颗粒被解析出亚基，其 RNA 核心被证明具催化性，现代义项由此固定。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): ribose itself is named from arabinose by reversing a letter, and the reason for that reversal is not documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ribose 之名是把 arabinose 颠倒一个字母而来，而这样颠倒的理由并无文献记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that share a piece with ribosome but name different objects; group two holds words for the same machinery seen from another angle.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ribosome 共享构件、但指不同对象的词；第二组是从另一角度命名同一套机器的词。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of the ribosome'. It describes RNA, proteins or sites, never the particle as a countable thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「核糖体的」，描述 RNA、蛋白或位点，不能作可数名词指颗粒本身。

entries.definition: An RNA molecule that catalyses a reaction, including the ribosome's own core. It is a molecule, not a particle.
entries.definitionCN: 具催化作用的 RNA 分子，包括核糖体自身的核心；是分子，不是颗粒。

entries.definition: The five-carbon sugar in RNA. It shares the ribo- piece but names a chemical, not a structure.
entries.definitionCN: RNA 中的五碳糖；共享 ribo- 构件，但指一种化学物质，不是结构。

entries.definition: A digestive organelle built with -some 'body'. Sharing the suffix does not make it part of translation.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -some「体」构成的消化细胞器；后缀相同，但与翻译无关。

entries.definition: Several ribosomes on one messenger RNA. It is the collective, while ribosome is one unit.
entries.definitionCN: 一条信使 RNA 上的多个核糖体；它是集合，ribosome 是单个单位。

entries.definition: Ribosomal RNA, the structural and catalytic core. It is a molecule inside the particle, not the particle.
entries.definitionCN: 核糖体 RNA，是结构与催化核心；它只是颗粒内部的分子。

entries.definition: Any specialised cell compartment. The ribosome is sometimes called one, though it lacks a membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何特化的细胞区室；核糖体有时也被称为细胞器，尽管它没有膜。

entries.definition: The whole process of making protein from messenger RNA, of which the ribosome is the site.
entries.definitionCN: 指由信使 RNA 制造蛋白质的全过程，核糖体是这一过程的场所。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ribo- (RNA) + -some (body): the RNA body that makes protein.
normal.cn: ribo-（RNA）+ -some（体）：造蛋白质的 RNA 之体。

normal.en: The family runs ribosome, ribosomal, rRNA, polysome, ribozyme.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ribosome、ribosomal、rRNA、polysome、ribozyme。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the parts: small subunit, large subunit, binding site, exit tunnel, polysome.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出部件：小亚基、大亚基、结合位点、出口通道、多聚核糖体。

normal.en: Two numbers separate the kingdoms: bacterial 70S, eukaryotic 80S.
normal.cn: 两个数字区分生物界：细菌 70S，真核 80S。

normal.en: The ribosome is a ribozyme at heart: its catalytic core is RNA, not protein.
normal.cn: 核糖体本质上是核酶：催化核心是 RNA，不是蛋白质。

abstract.en: Picture two uneven fists closing around a paper tape and reading it letter by letter.
abstract.cn: 想象两只大小不一的拳头夹住一条纸带，逐字读取。

abstract.en: Picture a workbench where a long instruction is copied into a string of beads.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工作台，把一条长指令抄成一串珠子。

abstract.en: Picture a factory so old that every later factory still uses its original jig.
abstract.cn: 想象一座工厂古老到后来所有工厂都仍在用它的原始夹具。

examples.en: Antibiotics that block the bacterial ribosome spare human cells.
examples.cn: 阻断细菌核糖体的抗生素不会伤害人体细胞。

examples.en: Ribosome profiling measures which messages are being translated at any moment.
examples.cn: 核糖体印迹测序测定任一时点正在被翻译的信使。

examples.en: Without functional ribosomes, a cell cannot replace its enzymes.
examples.cn: 没有功能正常的核糖体，细胞就无法更换自己的酶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来（ribo）一个身体（some）」——RNA 加蛋白组成的小身体，专门造蛋白 → 核糖体

root: ribo-（ribonucleic acid 的缩略，源自核糖 ribose）+ 希腊 soma「身体」（科学后缀 -some）→ 英语 ribosome（1950 年代）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a body made of RNA holds a tape and writes beads, and that writing is read as composition, as translation, as two halves, as a crowd, as a docking pad, as a drug target, and as a fossil.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一个由 RNA 构成的「体」夹住一条带子并写下珠子，而这次书写依次被读成组成、翻译、两半、群体、停靠处、药物靶点与化石。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lumps of RNA and protein gripping a tape and clicking beads into a chain.
core.cn: 核心意象：两团 RNA 与蛋白夹住一条带子，把珠子扣成链。

branches.en: THE NAMED PARTICLE: a body built of RNA is the literal coinage.
branches.cn: 被命名的颗粒：由 RNA 构成的「体」正是字面构造。

branches.en: MATERIAL: the particle is a mixture, so the name also covers its composition.
branches.cn: 材料：该颗粒是混合物，因此名称也覆盖其组成。

branches.en: THE WORK: reading a tape into a chain, done by two unequal halves.
branches.cn: 工作：把带子读成链，由大小不等的两半完成。

branches.en: MULTIPLICATION AND DOCKING: many particles on one tape, each landing on a site.
branches.cn: 倍增与停靠：一条带子上有多个颗粒，各自落在位点上。

branches.en: TARGET AND FOSSIL: the same particle is a place to intervene and a trace of early life.
branches.cn: 靶点与化石：同一个颗粒既是可介入的位置，也是早期生命的痕迹。

intro.en: Ribosome is a modern compound of a clipped chemical stem and a Greek noun; the parts are combining forms rather than a Latin root and suffix.
intro.cn: ribosome 是缩略的化学词干与希腊名词组成的现代合成词；其构件是组合形式，而非拉丁词根加后缀。

latinIntro.en: No inherited Latin source exists. The -some in ribosome is Greek soma 'body', and New Latin ribosoma is only a Latinized spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 没有传承的拉丁来源。ribosome 中的 -some 是希腊 soma「身体」，新拉丁语 ribosoma 只是拉丁化拼写。

items.meaningCN: 翻译用的 RNA-蛋白颗粒
items.example: Ribosomes cover the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
items.exampleCN: 核糖体布满粗面内质网。

items.example: Ribosomal proteins are assembled in the nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 核糖体蛋白在核内组装。

items.example: rRNA folds into the catalytic core.
items.exampleCN: rRNA 折叠成催化核心。

items.meaningCN: 一条信使上的多个核糖体
items.example: Polysomes cluster near the cell membrane.
items.exampleCN: 多聚核糖体聚集在细胞膜附近。

items.meaning: an RNA molecule with catalytic activity
items.meaningCN: 具催化活性的 RNA 分子
items.example: A ribozyme can cleave RNA without protein help.
items.exampleCN: 核酶无需蛋白帮助即可切割 RNA。

items.example: Ribonuclease cleared the sample of RNA.
items.exampleCN: 核糖核酸酶清除了样本中的 RNA。

items.meaning: the docking sequence on a message
items.example: A good binding site is needed for high yield.
items.exampleCN: 高产需要良好的结合位点。

items.meaning: sequencing the fragments protected by ribosomes
items.meaningCN: 对核糖体保护片段进行测序
items.example: Ribosome profiling revealed a hidden short gene.
items.exampleCN: 核糖体印迹揭示了一个隐藏的短基因。

definition_zh: 书写传统；以文字记录并延续的文本、知识与规范；书面传承本身
definition_en: the body of texts, and the practice of recording knowledge in writing, that a community carries forward
core_image: 一叠手抄本从书库传到抄书人案头，每一页都被重新誊写，页边添上新的批注
scene: 抄书人把旧手稿摊在案上，一笔一笔誊写，页边添上自己的批注，然后交给下一座书库。 A written tradition preserved the wording exactly, even when the meaning drifted.
sceneCN: 这里 written tradition 指以文字记录并延续的文本与做法（第 1 个义项：作为整体传统）；句意为书写传统把措辞原样保存下来，即使意思已经漂移。

pos.zh: 书写传统（可数，指某一群体的文本传统；不可数，指书面传承方式）

collocations.phrase: the written tradition of the church

derivatives.zh: 书写（古英语 writan「刻划、描画」，是本词组的基础动词）
写作者（由基础动词加表施事者的名词后缀而来，由动作转指施事的人）
书写；文字作品（由基础动词加表活动或产物的名词后缀而来，由动作转指活动或其产物）
令状；书面命令（古英语同一词形的直接继承，由「写下的东西」转指法律文书）
书面的（由基础动词的过去分词转作形容词，由动作转指已成文的状态）

senses.title: The carried body of texts
senses.definition: the whole collection of documents, books and records that a community keeps and passes on
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体保存并代代相传的全部文书、书籍与记录
senses.example: The monastery's written tradition fills forty cabinets.
senses.exampleCN: 这座修道院的书写传统装了四十个柜子。
senses.why: Tradition names what is handed down; written fixes the medium. Together they name a body of documents rather than one book.
senses.whyCN: 前者指被传下的东西，后者限定媒介；合起来命名的是一批文件，而不是某一本书。

senses.title: The practice of recording
senses.definition: the habit of committing events, rules and knowledge to writing
senses.definitionCN: 把事件、规则与知识写下来的习惯
senses.example: A strong written tradition began when the court hired full-time clerks.
senses.exampleCN: 当宫廷雇了专职书吏，一种强固的书写传统就开始了。
senses.why: Here the phrase names the activity rather than its products: the act of writing is what carries knowledge forward.
senses.whyCN: 这里命名的是活动而非产物：正是书写这个动作把知识带向未来。

senses.title: A canon or lineage of texts
senses.definition: a recognised set of authoritative texts that later writers comment on and inherit
senses.definitionCN: 一套被承认的权威文本，后来的写作者对它注释并继承
senses.example: Later poets measured themselves against the written tradition of the epic.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的诗人以史诗的书写传统来衡量自己。
senses.why: Once texts are fixed, they can be ranked and commented on, and the phrase comes to mean a canon with a family tree.
senses.whyCN: 文本一旦固定，就能被排序与注释，这个词组于是指一棵有家谱的经典谱系。

senses.title: Legal and administrative records
senses.definition: the documentary habit of courts, temples and offices that keeps decisions in writing
senses.definitionCN: 法庭、神庙与官署把决定留在纸面上的文书习惯
senses.example: Land disputes were settled by consulting the written tradition of the county.
senses.exampleCN: 土地纠纷靠查阅该县的文书传统来解决。
senses.why: Administration needs a memory that outlives officials; written records supply exactly that, so the phrase covers archives of rule.
senses.whyCN: 行政需要一种比官员活得久的记忆；书面记录正好提供它，因此这个词组覆盖统治的档案。

senses.title: Scholarship built on citation
senses.definition: research that advances by quoting, correcting and adding to earlier written work
senses.definitionCN: 通过引用、修正与增补前人文字而推进的研究
senses.example: The field grew out of a written tradition of marginal notes.
senses.exampleCN: 这个领域从页边批注的书写传统中生长出来。
senses.why: Citation makes scholarship cumulative: each text stands on the page of another, and the phrase names that chain.
senses.whyCN: 引用使学术可以累积：每篇文字都站在另一篇的纸页上，这个词组命名的正是这条链。

senses.title: Literacy and print culture
senses.definition: the social stage in which reading and writing organise public life
senses.definitionCN: 阅读与书写组织公共生活的社会阶段
senses.example: Print turned a narrow written tradition into a mass one.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷把狭窄的书写传统变成了大众传统。
senses.why: The phrase can mark a whole social condition, set against an oral culture where most people never read.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组可以标记一整个社会状况，与多数人不识字的口头文化相对。

senses.title: Fixity of wording
senses.definition: the property that a text keeps the same words each time it is read
senses.definitionCN: 文本每次被阅读时都保持同样措辞的性质
senses.example: A written tradition can preserve a formula for a thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 书写传统能把一个固定说法保存一千年。
senses.why: Writing freezes wording, so the phrase also names the exactness that speech cannot guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 书写冻结措辞，因此这个词组也命名言谈无法保证的那种精确。

senses.title: The critique of what writing leaves out
senses.titleCN: 对书写遗漏之物的批判
senses.definition: the argument that written records favour the literate, the powerful and the official
senses.definitionCN: 认为书面记录偏袒识字者、掌权者与官方视角的论点
senses.example: Historians now ask what the written tradition silenced.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学者现在会问书写传统让什么沉默了。
senses.why: Because only some voices reach the page, the phrase can also name the blind spot produced by writing itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为只有部分嗓音能到纸面，这个词组也能命名书写本身造成的盲区。

intro.en: Written is the past participle of write, from Old English writan 'to score, outline, scratch'. Tradition comes from Latin traditio 'a handing over'. The English phrase contrasts with oral tradition in folklore and classics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: written 是 write 的过去分词，源自古英语 writan「刻划、描画、勾出轮廓」。tradition 来自拉丁 traditio「递交」。这个英语词组在民俗学与古典学中与口头传统相对。年代均为约数。

items.en: Writan was a strong verb meaning 'to score, outline, draw the figure of', with past tense wrat and past participle writen. Its earliest sense was cutting marks into a surface.
items.cn: writan 是强变化动词，意为「刻划、勾轮廓、描画形状」，过去式 wrat，过去分词 writen。最早的意义是把痕迹刻进表面。

items.en: The reconstructed ancestor is *writan 'to tear, scratch', a reconstruction attested by the older Germanic forms rather than by any written record.
items.cn: 重构的祖词是 *writan「撕、抓、刻」，这一形式靠更早的日耳曼语形式推得，并无直接书证。

items.en: The usual reconstruction is *wreid- 'to cut, scratch'. The reconstruction is secure for Germanic but its links outside Germanic are not established.
items.cn: 通行的重构是 *wreid-「切、刻」。这一重构在日耳曼语内部较可靠，但与日耳曼语之外的关联尚未证实。

items.en: Tradere 'to hand over' is trans- 'across' plus dare 'to give'; its noun traditio first meant delivery and then teaching handed down.
items.cn: tradere「递交」由表示「穿过」的前缀加 dare「给」构成；其名词 traditio 先指交付，再指传下的教导。

items.en: Written tradition became a standard counterpart to oral tradition in the nineteenth century, when collectors and classicists compared literate and spoken cultures.
items.cn: 十九世纪，written tradition 成为 oral tradition 的标准对应说法，当时收集者与古典学者开始比较文字文化与口说文化。

items.en: Source uncertain: the shape of the reconstructed Indo-European root is a reconstruction, and the older history of tradere's components beyond the transparent prefix and verb is not recoverable.
items.cn: 来源不确定：所重构的原始印欧语词根形状属重构形式；tradere 除清楚可见的前缀与动词外，更早的构件历史已不可考。

note.en: Group one separates forms of the verb write; group two holds textual and archival neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词 write 的各种形式；第二组是文本与档案方面的近邻词。

entries.definition: The act of writing or the marks produced; it can name a single piece of work, not an inherited body.
entries.definitionCN: 书写动作或写出的痕迹；可以指单件作品，而非继承的整体。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: put down on paper. It describes a thing, not a tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词：写在纸上的。它描述某物，而非一种传统。

entries.definition: A formal written order from a court; the spelling lost the final e and narrowed to law.
entries.definitionCN: 法庭的正式书面命令；拼写丢了词尾的 e，词义收窄到法律。

entries.definition: One who writes; the suffix marks the agent, while the phrase marks the inherited corpus.
entries.definitionCN: 写作的人；后缀标记施事，而词组标记继承下来的文本总体。

entries.definition: The chain of hand-copied copies through which a text survives; narrower than written tradition, which includes print.
entries.definitionCN: 文本靠手抄副本延续的链条；比书写传统窄，后者还包括印刷。

entries.definition: The study of how a text's wording changed across copies; it focuses on variants rather than on writing as a habit.
entries.definitionCN: 研究文本措辞在各副本间如何变化；它关注异文，而非书写习惯本身。

entries.definition: The social world shaped by movable type; it is a later stage within a written tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 由活字印刷塑造的社会世界；它是书写传统内部较晚的阶段。

entries.definition: The individual documents left behind; the tradition is the continuing practice that produced them.
entries.definitionCN: 留下的具体文件；而传统是产生这些文件的持续做法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Old English verb, its surviving forms and real archival phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的古英语动词、它留存的形式与真实的档案说法。

normal.en: Write first meant to scratch a mark; writing began as cutting, not as ink.
normal.cn: write 最初意为刻痕；书写一开始是刻，而不是蘸墨。

normal.en: The same verb yields writer, writing, writ and written, each pointing at a different part of the act.
normal.cn: 同一个动词给出 writer、writing、writ、written，各自指向动作的不同部分。

normal.en: Tradition is a handing over, so a written tradition is a handing over done on paper.
normal.cn: tradition 是递交，所以书写传统就是在纸上完成的递交。

normal.en: Fixed phrases set the contrast: written tradition and oral memory, a long written tradition.
normal.cn: 固定说法建立对比：书写传统与口头记忆、悠久的书写传统。

normal.en: The plural written traditions fits comparisons between churches, courts or schools.
normal.cn: 比较教会、宫廷或学派时，复数 written traditions 合适。

abstract.en: Picture a page that never forgets but also never notices who was left out.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸，它从不遗忘，却也从不注意谁被漏掉了。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of copyists, each adding one marginal note that later readers treat as part of the text.
abstract.cn: 想象一串抄写者，每人添一条页边批注，后来的读者却把它当作正文的一部分。

abstract.en: Picture a law that outlives every official who wrote it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条法律，比写下它的每位官员都活得久。

examples.en: The island's written tradition begins with ships' logs and church registers.
examples.cn: 这座岛的书写传统始于航海日志与教会登记簿。

examples.en: A written tradition can preserve a name long after the language around it changes.
examples.cn: 书写传统能在周围语言改变很久之后仍保存一个名字。

examples.en: Critics ask whose voices never entered the written tradition.
examples.cn: 批评者追问哪些人的声音从未进入书写传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: written（写下的）+ tradition（递交）＝ 用文字一页页交下去的东西；记「刻痕变墨迹，墨迹变档案」。

root: written 源自古英语 writan「刻划、描画」，其过去分词为 written，更早的日耳曼语与原始印欧语形式均属重构；tradition 源自拉丁 traditio「递交」，来自动词 tradere，该动词由前缀表「穿过」加 dare「给」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the corpus itself to the habit of writing, then to canon, archive, scholarship, literacy, fixity and the criticism of what the page excludes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从文本总体移向书写习惯，再到经典、档案、学术、识字、固定性，以及对纸页排除之物的批判。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand copying a page so that the same words arrive in a later century.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手誊抄一页，让同样的字句抵达另一个世纪。

branches.en: CORPUS AND HABIT: the collected texts, and the repeated act of writing them down.
branches.cn: 总体与习惯：收集起来的文本，以及反复把它们写下的动作。

branches.en: CANON AND FIXITY: ranking texts requires that their wording stop changing.
branches.cn: 经典与固定：要给文本排序，先得让措辞不再变动。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: courts and offices keep decisions alive on paper.
branches.cn: 账册：法庭与官署靠纸面让决定继续活着。

branches.en: CITATION: scholarship grows by standing each text on the page of another.
branches.cn: 引用：学术靠让每篇文字站上另一篇的纸页而生长。

branches.en: LITERACY AND ITS BLIND SPOT: a reading public, and the voices that never reached it.
branches.cn: 识字及其盲区：一个阅读公众，以及从未抵达它的那些声音。

intro.en: The phrase combines an Old English verb with a Latin noun: the first half is native, the second borrowed.
intro.cn: 这个词组把古英语动词与拉丁名词组合起来：前半是本族语，后半是借词。

latinIntro.en: Only tradition is Latin; write and its forms descend from Old English and have no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 tradition 属拉丁来源；write 及其各种形式源自古英语，没有拉丁来源。

items.meaning: to make marks that record words
items.meaningCN: 书写；留下记录文字的痕迹
items.example: She writes in a small notebook every night.
items.exampleCN: 她每晚在一个小本子上写字。

items.example: The writer revised the chapter twice.
items.exampleCN: 作者把这一章改了两遍。

items.meaning: the act of writing or what is written
items.example: His writing is clear and compact.
items.exampleCN: 他的文字清楚而紧凑。

items.example: A written answer is required.
items.exampleCN: 要求提交书面答复。

items.example: The court issued a writ of summons.
items.exampleCN: 法庭发出了传唤令状。

items.example: The tradition dates from the first abbey.
items.exampleCN: 这一传统始于第一座修道院。

items.example: Traditional records were kept in Latin.
items.exampleCN: 传统记录用拉丁文保存。

items.example: Monks transcribed the old pages by hand.
items.exampleCN: 修士们手工誊写那些旧页。

items.example: The manuscript survived in one copy.
items.exampleCN: 这份手稿只靠一个副本留存。

definition_zh: 醋酸盐；醋酸酯；醋酸纤维（片基）
definition_en: a salt or ester of acetic acid, or a synthetic material made from cellulose acetate
core_image: 实验室架上并排摆着醋酸盐晶体与一卷透明胶片
scene: 实验室的架子上，一边是白色晶体，一边是卷起来的透明薄片。 The acetate film was stored in a dry cabinet.
sceneCN: 这里 acetate 是「醋酸片基、醋酸纤维」（第 2 个义项：由醋酸纤维素制成的材料）；句意为这种醋酸胶片存放在干燥柜里。

pos.zh: 醋酸盐；醋酸酯
醋酸纤维；醋酸片基

derivatives.zh: 同源形容词，义为「醋酸的」

senses.title: A salt or ester of acetic acid
senses.definition: a chemical compound formed from acetic acid and a base or an alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 醋酸与碱或醇反应生成的化合物
senses.example: Sodium acetate buffers the solution against pH change.
senses.exampleCN: 醋酸钠让溶液在酸碱度变化时保持稳定。
senses.why: The -ate ending marks the salt or ester made from an acid, so acetate is literally 'the vinegar salt'.
senses.whyCN: -ate 后缀标记由酸生成的盐或酯，因此 acetate 字面就是「醋的盐」。

senses.title: A synthetic fibre or film base
senses.definition: a material made from cellulose acetate, used for fibres, film, and plastic
senses.definitionCN: 由醋酸纤维素制成，用于纤维、胶片与塑料的材料
senses.example: The old photographs were printed on acetate film.
senses.exampleCN: 这些老照片印在醋酸胶片上。
senses.why: The chemical name shifted to the material itself: cellulose treated with acetic acid becomes a clear film.
senses.whyCN: 化学名称转指材料本身：纤维素经醋酸处理后变成透明薄片。

senses.title: A recording disc
senses.definition: a thin disc coated with acetate, used to record sound
senses.definitionCN: 表面涂有醋酸层的薄唱片，用于录制声音
senses.example: The engineer cut the session onto an acetate disc.
senses.exampleCN: 录音师把这次录音刻到一张醋酸唱片上。
senses.why: In studios the same transparent layer became a master disc for sound.
senses.whyCN: 在录音室里，同一种透明涂层成了声音的母盘。

intro.en: Acetate comes from Latin acetum, 'vinegar', with the chemical ending -ate; the acid in vinegar gave the name to its salts.
intro.cn: acetate 来自拉丁语 acetum（醋），加上化学后缀 -ate；醋里的酸把名字给了它的盐。

items.en: acetum meant 'vinegar', a sour liquid made from wine.
items.cn: acetum 意为「醋」，一种由酒变酸的液体。

items.en: acere meant 'to be sour', the verb behind acid and acetic.
items.cn: acere 意为「有酸味」，是 acid 与 acetic 背后的动词。

items.en: aceticus meant 'of vinegar', the source of acetic.
items.cn: aceticus 意为「醋的」，是 acetic 的来源。

items.en: chemists named the salts of vinegar acid acetates.
items.cn: 化学家在十八世纪把醋酸生成的盐命名为 acetate。

items.en: English applied acetate to cellulose film and fibre.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪把 acetate 用于醋酸纤维素胶片与纤维。

items.en: modern usage keeps both the chemical and the material senses.
items.cn: 现代用法同时保留化学义与材料义。

note.en: The first group gathers related chemical words; the second gathers other salts and esters.
note.cn: 第一组收相关化学词；第二组收其他盐类与酯类。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「醋酸的」

entries.definition: The chemical group derived from acetic acid.

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the vinegar root and the film material; the abstract hooks picture crystals beside a clear film roll.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「醋」词根与胶片材料；抽象记忆点想象晶体旁边放着一卷透明胶片。

normal.en: Acetate is 'vinegar salt': acetum means vinegar.
normal.cn: acetate 是「醋的盐」：acetum 意为醋。

normal.en: Cellulose acetate is the material behind film and fibre.
normal.cn: cellulose acetate 是胶片与纤维背后的材料。

normal.en: The ending -ate signals a salt or an ester.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ate 表示盐或酯。

normal.en: Acetic is the adjective; acetate is the noun.
normal.cn: acetic 是形容词，acetate 是名词。

normal.en: In studios an acetate is a master recording disc.
normal.cn: 在录音室里，an acetate 指母盘唱片。

abstract.en: Picture white crystals beside a roll of clear film.
abstract.cn: 想象白色晶体旁边放着一卷透明胶片。

abstract.en: Picture a label reading sodium acetate on a reagent bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象试剂瓶上贴着醋酸钠的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a studio engineer cutting a disc.
abstract.cn: 想象录音师在刻录一张唱片。

examples.en: The buffer was prepared with sodium acetate.
examples.cn: 缓冲液是用醋酸钠配制的。

examples.en: Cellulose acetate is used to make photographic film.
examples.cn: 醋酸纤维素用于制造照相胶片。

examples.en: Acetate fibres dry quickly and hold colour well.
examples.cn: 醋酸纤维干得快，固色也好。

sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从化学上的盐或酯，走到合成胶片材料，再到录音盘。

definition_zh: 食虫的；以昆虫为食的
definition_en: feeding chiefly on insects
core_image: 一片叶子合拢，把落脚的苍蝇裹进消化液
scene: 这里指「食虫的」。 The sundew is an insectivorous plant that digests flies on its sticky leaves.
sceneCN: 这里 insectivorous 是「食虫的」（第 2 个义项：植物捕食并消化昆虫）；句意：茅膏菜是食虫植物，用黏性叶片消化苍蝇。

pos.zh: 食虫的；以昆虫为食的；（旧分类）食虫目的

senses.title: Living on insects
senses.definition: describing an animal whose diet is made up mostly of insects
senses.definitionCN: 描述以昆虫为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Insectivorous bats emerge at dusk to hunt moths over the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 食虫蝙蝠在黄昏时飞出，在果园上方捕食飞蛾。
senses.why: The suffix -ous turns the noun insectivore into a description, so the diet becomes a property of the animal.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ous 把名词 insectivore 变成描述性形容词，于是食性成了动物的一种属性。

senses.title: Plants that catch and digest
senses.definition: describing a plant that traps insects and absorbs nutrients from them
senses.definitionCN: 描述捕捉昆虫并从中吸收养分的植物
senses.example: Insectivorous leaves often lose their trapping colour in shady conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 食虫植物的叶片在遮阴条件下常会失去捕虫的颜色。
senses.why: Botany applies the human-scale eater to a plant, and the adjective lets the plant modify leaf, species or habitat.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把「取食者」这一人间尺度套用到植物，形容词形式便于直接修饰 leaf、species 或 habitat。

senses.title: Of the old order Insectivora
senses.definition: in older taxonomy, belonging to the mammalian order Insectivora
senses.definitionCN: 旧分类学中属于哺乳动物食虫目的
senses.example: The insectivorous families were later split across several orders.
senses.exampleCN: 这些食虫目科后来被拆散到多个目之中。
senses.why: Taxonomic adjectives follow the order name, so the food word became a formal classifier before the order was dissolved.
senses.whyCN: 分类学形容词跟着目名走，因此这个「食物词」在该目被撤销之前先成了一个正式分类标签。

senses.title: Built for an insect diet
senses.definition: describing teeth, jaws or guts shaped for catching and digesting insects
senses.definitionCN: 描述为捕捉与消化昆虫而演化出的牙齿、颌骨或消化道
senses.example: The fossil shows the insectivorous dentition typical of small nocturnal hunters.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石显示出小型夜行捕食者典型的食虫齿列。
senses.why: Anatomy needs a word for structures that serve a diet, and the adjective attaches to the part rather than the whole animal.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学需要一个词来描述「为某种食性服务的结构」，形容词便附着在部位而不是整个动物身上。

senses.title: An ecological label
senses.definition: classifying a species by its membership in the insect-eating guild
senses.definitionCN: 按其在食虫功能群中的归属来分类物种
senses.example: The insectivorous birds shifted to fruit when caterpillars disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 毛虫消失后，这些食虫鸟转而取食果实。
senses.why: Ecology uses adjectives to tag feeding roles quickly, so a species can be insectivorous in one season and not in another.
senses.whyCN: 生态学用形容词快速标注取食角色，因此同一物种在不同季节可以是食虫的，也可以不是。

senses.title: A pest-control ally
senses.definition: used of species valued because they suppress insect pests
senses.definitionCN: 用于指因抑制害虫而受重视的物种
senses.example: Farmers encourage insectivorous birds by keeping hedges and water.
senses.exampleCN: 农民保留树篱与水源，以招引食虫鸟。
senses.why: Applied writing converts the diet into a benefit, and the adjective marks the useful side of the same habit.
senses.whyCN: 应用写作把食性转化为效益，形容词标出的正是同一习性的有用一面。

senses.title: A trophic position
senses.definition: placed at the trophic level of consumers that feed on insects
senses.definitionCN: 处于以昆虫为食的消费者营养级
senses.example: Insectivorous fish link aquatic insects to larger predators.
senses.exampleCN: 食虫鱼类把水生昆虫连接到更大的捕食者。
senses.why: Food-web models need a level label, and the adjective marks where energy from insects enters the next trophic step.
senses.whyCN: 食物网模型需要一个层级标签，形容词标出的是昆虫的能量进入下一营养级的位置。

senses.title: Of peoples who eat insects
senses.definition: describing human communities whose traditional diet regularly includes insects
senses.definitionCN: 描述传统饮食中经常包含昆虫的人类群体
senses.example: Anthropologists documented insectivorous practices across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 人类学家记录了该地区各地的食虫习俗。
senses.why: The adjective's pattern extends to human groups, where it labels a cultural diet rather than a biological adaptation.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词的模式也延伸到人类群体，在那里标出的是文化性的饮食，而不是生物学适应。

intro.en: Insectivorous is the adjective built on insectivore, with a Latin ending that turns a noun of agent into a description.
intro.cn: insectivorous 是在 insectivore 基础上构成的形容词，用拉丁语词尾把「施动者名词」变成描述语。

items.en: The base is insectum, 'a thing cut into', plus vorare, 'to devour'. Both belonged to ordinary Latin before science borrowed them.
items.cn: 词基是 insectum「被切开的东西」加 vorare「吞食」。在被科学借用之前，这两个词都属于普通拉丁语。

items.en: The ending -ous continues Latin -osus, 'full of, characterized by'. It does not mean 'eating' by itself; the meaning is carried by the stem.
items.cn: 词尾 -ous 承自拉丁语 -osus「充满……的、以……为特征的」。它本身不表示「吃」，意义由词干承担。

items.en: Naturalists needed adjectives for diet-based groups, and insectivorous appeared alongside carnivorous and graminivorous in the same period.
items.cn: 博物学家需要为按食性划分的类群准备形容词，insectivorous 与 carnivorous、graminivorous 大约在同一时期出现。

items.en: Victorian botany popularized insectivorous plant after collectors brought back sundews and pitcher plants from tropical voyages.
items.cn: 维多利亚时代的植物学使 insectivorous plant 流行起来，当时采集者从热带航行带回茅膏菜与猪笼草。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology kept the adjective for functional and trophic labels, where diet is a role rather than a fixed identity.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生态学保留了这个形容词，用于功能群与营养级标签，此时食性是角色而非固定身份。

note.en: The first group is built from the same pieces; the second holds adjectives for other diets.
note.cn: 第一组由相同成分构成；第二组是表示其他食性的形容词。

entries.definition: The creature itself; insectivorous is the form that modifies bird, plant or dentition.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物本身；修饰 bird、plant、dentition 时要用 insectivorous。

entries.definition: The habit or diet, not a describer; you study insectivory but describe an insectivorous species.
entries.definitionCN: 指习性饮食，不是描述语；可以说研究 insectivory，但描述物种要用 insectivorous。

entries.definition: The food item; it says nothing about the eater's diet as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指食物本身，不说明取食者的整体食性。

entries.definition: Feeding on animal flesh; insects count as animal prey, so insectivorous is a narrow kind of carnivorous.
entries.definitionCN: 以动物肉体为食；昆虫也算动物性猎物，因此食虫是食肉的一种窄义。

entries.definition: Feeding on plants; the opposite dietary pole, though some insectivorous plants still photosynthesize.
entries.definitionCN: 以植物为食，是食性上的另一端；不过有些食虫植物仍进行光合作用。

entries.definition: Eating both plant and animal matter; such an animal may be insectivorous only part of the year.
entries.definitionCN: 动植物都吃；这类动物可能只在一年中的部分时间食虫。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the same Latin pieces seen from the adjective side.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：从形容词一侧看同一批拉丁语成分。

normal.en: -ous is the adjective switch: insectivore becomes insectivorous.
normal.cn: -ous 是形容词开关：insectivore 变成 insectivorous。

normal.en: The collocations mirror biology: insectivorous plant, bird, mammal, diet.
normal.cn: 搭配对应生物学场景：食虫植物、食虫鸟、食虫哺乳动物、食虫食性。

normal.en: The word sits in a family of diet adjectives: carnivorous, herbivorous, omnivorous.
normal.cn: 这个词属于一组食性形容词：carnivorous、herbivorous、omnivorous。

normal.en: A sundew is the clearest picture: a leaf that behaves like a stomach.
normal.cn: 茅膏菜是最清楚的画面：一片像胃一样工作的叶子。

normal.en: The first half is the prey, the second half is the eating; the ending says 'characterized by'.
normal.cn: 前半是猎物，后半是吃；词尾表示「以……为特征」。

abstract.en: Think of a restaurant whose only supplier is the insect world.
abstract.cn: 想象一家唯一供货商是昆虫世界的餐厅。

abstract.en: Picture a sticky doormat that punishes whoever steps on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块黏性门垫，谁踩上去谁就倒霉。

abstract.en: An insectivorous bird is a flying insect net that digests its catch.
abstract.cn: 食虫鸟就是一张会飞的昆虫网，还会把捕到的东西消化掉。

examples.en: Insectivorous birds help keep the orchard's caterpillars in check.
examples.cn: 食虫鸟有助于控制果园里的毛虫数量。

examples.en: The plant's insectivorous habit evolved in nutrient-poor bogs.
examples.cn: 这种植物的食虫习性是在养分贫乏的沼泽中演化出来的。

examples.en: Researchers compared the insectivorous diets of two bat species.
examples.cn: 研究者比较了两种蝙蝠的食虫食性。

dict_mnemonic.text: insect（昆虫）+ vor（吞）+ ous（……的）→ 吞昆虫的 → 食虫的

root: 拉丁语 insectum「昆虫」+ vorare「吞食」+ 形容词后缀 -ous（拉丁 -osus「充满……的」）→ insectivorous「以昆虫为食的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same property from different angles: the animal, the plant, the old order, the anatomy, the guild, the pest-control benefit, the trophic level and human communities.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从不同角度描述同一属性：动物、植物、旧分类目、解剖结构、功能群、害虫防治效益、营养级与人类群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a diet made of insects, attached to whatever lives on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：以昆虫构成的食谱，附着在任何靠它生活的生物身上。

branches.en: THE CORE: the adjective turns the noun insectivore into a property, whether the eater is an animal or an order member.
branches.cn: 核心：形容词把名词 insectivore 变成一种属性，无论取食者是动物还是旧目成员。

branches.en: THE PLANT: botany applies the same property to a photosynthesizing organism that traps prey.
branches.cn: 植物：植物学把同一属性用在一种仍进行光合作用、却能捕捉猎物的生物上。

branches.en: BODY AND LEVEL: the diet can be read from teeth or placed as a trophic position.
branches.cn: 身体与层级：食性既可以从牙齿读出，也能被放进营养级的位置。

branches.en: ROLE AND BENEFIT: ecology turns the diet into a guild label, and agriculture turns it into a service.
branches.cn: 角色与效益：生态学把食性变成功能群标签，农业把它变成一项服务。

branches.en: HUMANS: the same adjective can describe a cultural diet rather than a biological one.
branches.cn: 人类：同一形容词可以描述文化性的饮食，而不是生物学食性。

intro.en: Insectivorous is a three-part word: prey noun, eating root, descriptive ending.
intro.cn: insectivorous 由三部分组成：猎物名词、表示吃的词根、描述性词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are insectum and vorare, with the adjective ending -osus giving English -ous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 insectum 与 vorare，形容词词尾 -osus 在英语中变成 -ous。

items.example: The insectivorous bird nests in hollow trees.
items.exampleCN: 这种食虫鸟在空心树里筑巢。

items.example: The insectivore stores fat for the cold months.
items.exampleCN: 这种食虫动物为寒冷月份储存脂肪。

items.example: Insectivory is common among small tropical birds.
items.exampleCN: 食虫习性在小型热带鸟类中很常见。

items.example: Carnivorous plants trap more than insects.
items.exampleCN: 食肉植物捕捉的不只是昆虫。

items.example: Herbivorous insects strip the leaves in weeks.
items.exampleCN: 食草昆虫几周内就能把叶子吃光。

items.example: The nestlings have voracious appetites.
items.exampleCN: 雏鸟的食量很大。

items.example: The trap catches insects by smell.
items.exampleCN: 这个诱捕器靠气味捕捉昆虫。

items.example: The label warns that the insecticide harms bees.
items.exampleCN: 标签警告这种杀虫剂会伤害蜜蜂。

definition_zh: n. 猛攻；袭击；侵犯人身罪；v. 袭击；猛烈抨击
definition_en: A sudden violent attack, or the crime of attacking or threatening someone; as a verb, to attack physically or to criticise fiercely.
core_image: 一只手突然挥过来，或者一道防线被硬生生撞开
scene: 他因在酒吧外动手伤人被起诉。 He was charged with assault outside the bar.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：assault 在法律上指侵犯人身的罪名，不一定要造成重伤。

pos.zh: 猛攻；袭击；侵犯人身罪
袭击；猛烈抨击

senses.title: A sudden violent attack
senses.definition: a forceful attack on a person or a place, the older military and physical sense
senses.definitionCN: 对人或地点的强力攻击，是较早的军事与身体义
senses.example: The assault on the walls began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 对城墙的猛攻在黎明开始。
senses.why: The root means to leap, so an assault is a jump at a wall or a body rather than a slow siege.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「跳」，所以 assault 是朝城墙或身体的一跃，而不是缓慢的围困。

senses.title: The crime against a person
senses.definition: in law, an act that attacks or threatens another person, which need not cause serious injury
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指攻击或威胁他人的行为，不必造成重伤
senses.example: He pleaded guilty to common assault.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认普通侵犯人身罪。
senses.why: The legal sense narrowed the word to a defined offence, which is why it appears in charges and reports.
senses.whyCN: 法律义把这个词收窄为一项确定的罪名，所以它出现在起诉与判决书中。

senses.title: To attack or criticise fiercely
senses.definition: as a verb, to attack someone physically, or to attack a policy or idea in strong terms
senses.definitionCN: 作动词指动手袭击某人，或用强烈言辞攻击某项政策或观点
senses.example: The report assaults the whole funding model.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告猛攻整套资助模式。
senses.why: The verb keeps both fronts open, so a policy can be assaulted exactly as a gate can.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词两条战线都留着，所以一项政策可以像一道城门那样被 assault。

intro.en: Assault is Latin assultus, from assilire, to leap at, formed from ad, at, plus salire, to leap; Old French asaut lost the l that scholars later restored.
intro.cn: assault 就是拉丁语 assultus，出自 assilire「扑向」，由 ad「向」加 salire「跳」构成；古法语 asaut 丢掉的 l 后来被学者补回。

items.en: Latin salire meant to leap, the physical core shared with assail and salient.
items.cn: 拉丁语 salire 意为「跳」，是与 assail、salient 共有的身体内核。

items.en: With ad, at, assilire meant to spring upon, and its noun assultus named the springing.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」后，assilire 意为「跃上」，其名词 assultus 指那一跃。

items.en: Old French asaut meant a violent attack and dropped the l of the Latin form.
items.cn: 古法语 asaut 意为猛攻，并丢掉了拉丁形式中的 l。

items.en: Middle English assaut named both a military storming and a personal attack.
items.cn: 中古英语 assaut 既指军事强攻，也指对人身的攻击。

items.en: Sixteenth-century writers put the l back to match Latin, giving the modern spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪的书写者为对齐拉丁语把 l 补回，形成现代拼写。

items.en: English law then fixed assault as a named offence, distinct from the actual striking called battery.
items.cn: 此后英国法把 assault 定为一项罪名，与实际动手的 battery 相区别。

note.en: The look-alike group warns that result, insult and consult only share sounds; the near-meaning group separates the attack, the ambush and the legal pair.
note.cn: 形近组提醒 result、insult、consult 只是音近；近义组把猛攻、伏击与法律上的一对罪名分开。

entries.definition: To attack or trouble strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈攻击或强烈困扰。

entries.definition: Something that follows from a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 由某个原因带来的结果。

entries.definition: To speak or act rudely towards someone.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人言语或举止无礼。

entries.definition: To seek advice from someone.
entries.definitionCN: 向某人征求意见。

entries.definition: A violent act against someone.
entries.definitionCN: 针对某人的暴力行为。

entries.definition: A fierce and sustained attack.
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈而持续的攻击。

entries.definition: A surprise attack from a hiding place.
entries.definitionCN: 从藏身处发起的突袭。

entries.definition: The crime of unlawful physical contact.
entries.definitionCN: 非法动手接触他人的罪名。

normalIntro.en: Assault is the noun cousin of assail: the same leap at a target, frozen into a thing you can name in court.
normalIntro.cn: assault 是 assail 的名词表亲：同样朝目标一跃，只是被定格成能在法庭上指称的一件事。

normal.en: An assault on something is the usual pattern.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 an assault on something。

normal.en: In law, assault and battery are different charges.
normal.cn: 法律上 assault 与 battery 是不同罪名。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object: assault a guard.
normal.cn: 动词直接带宾语：assault a guard。

normal.en: Assail is the verb form with the same root.
normal.cn: assail 是同根的动词形式。

normal.en: The l was put back to look like Latin.
normal.cn: 那个 l 是为了像拉丁语才补回的。

abstract.en: Picture a hand swinging before you can step back.
abstract.cn: 想象你还来不及后退就挥过来的一只手。

abstract.en: Imagine ladders hitting a wall at first light.
abstract.cn: 想象天刚亮就搭上城墙的梯子。

abstract.en: Think of a report landing like a blow.
abstract.cn: 想象一份报告像拳头一样落下。

examples.en: The assault left the door hanging open.
examples.cn: 猛攻之后门被撞得敞着。

examples.en: She reported the assault to the police.
examples.cn: 她向警方报了这起袭击。

examples.en: Columnists assaulted the new tax.
examples.cn: 专栏作者猛攻新税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：as-「向」+ sault「跳」——朝人跃过去的那一下，就是袭击 assault；同根动词是 assail。

root: 拉丁语 salire「跳」加 ad-「向」构成 assilire「扑向」，名词 assultus 经古法语 asaut 入英语，十六世纪补回 l 成 assault；十七世纪法律把它定为罪名。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are one leap at a target: storming a wall, the offence named in a charge, and the verb that does it to bodies or to policies.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都是朝目标的一次扑击：强攻城墙、起诉状里的罪名，以及作用于身体或政策的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand swinging out, or a line forced open
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手突然挥过来，或一道防线被硬生生撞开

branches.cn: 黎明搭上城墙的梯子。

branches.cn: 像拳头一样落下的报告。

branches.en: One leap, named as act, offence and verb.
branches.cn: 同一次扑击，被称作行为、罪名与动词。

intro.en: Assault is as- from ad- plus -sault from salire, leap; the same root builds assail, salient, insult and result.
intro.cn: assault 由 ad- 变来的 as- 加出自 salire「跳」的 -sault 构成；同一词根还构成 assail、salient、insult 与 result。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is salire, to leap, assilire, to leap at, and assultus, the leap itself; the agent ending -ant gives assailant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 salire「跳」、assilire「扑向」与 assultus「那一跃」；施事后缀 -ant 给出 assailant。

definition_zh: 哺乳动物的；哺乳动物个体；哺乳类生理特征的；哺乳动物演化与区系的；哺乳动物式的（温情照护）
definition_en: belonging to the class of animals that suckle their young, or describing a member, a trait, a lineage, a laboratory model or a regional fauna drawn from that class
core_image: 一只母兽侧卧，幼崽贴住它的腹部吃奶，两个体温合成一块暖区
scene: 标本室里，一排骨架从鼩鼱排到鲸鱼，每副都挂着同一类群的标签。 Every skeleton in the drawer carries a label marking it as mammalian, whatever its size.
sceneCN: 这里 mammalian 是「哺乳动物的」（第 1 个义项：分类学上属于哺乳纲的）；句意：抽屉里每副骨架都贴着标明它属于哺乳动物的标签，无论体型大小。

pos.zh: 哺乳动物的；哺乳纲的
哺乳动物（动物学专业用法，可数，复数 mammalians）

senses.title: Of the Class Mammalia
senses.definition: belonging to Mammalia, the class of vertebrates that have hair and suckle their young
senses.definitionCN: 属于哺乳纲的，即体表有毛、以乳汁哺育幼崽的脊椎动物类群
senses.example: The mammalian skull differs from the reptilian one in its jaw joint.
senses.exampleCN: 哺乳动物的头骨在颌关节处与爬行动物的头骨不同。
senses.why: Mammalia is the taxonomic name Linnaeus gave the class, so the adjective simply labels membership in it.
senses.whyCN: Mammalia 是林奈为这一纲所立的分类名，形容词因此只负责标明「属于该纲」。

senses.title: A Member of the Class
senses.definition: as a noun, one animal belonging to Mammalia
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时，指属于哺乳纲的一个动物个体
senses.example: Each mammalian in the sample was weighed before release.
senses.exampleCN: 样本中的每只哺乳动物都在放归前称了重。
senses.why: zoologists routinely turn class adjectives into countable nouns, so the adjective can stand for the animal itself.
senses.whyCN: 动物学家惯于把纲的形容词用作可数名词，这个形容词因此能直接指那只动物。

senses.title: Of the Defining Traits
senses.definition: describing the warm-blooded, milk-producing, live-bearing traits that define the class
senses.definitionCN: 描述恒温、泌乳、胎生这些界定该纲的生理特征
senses.example: Mammalian warmth comes from a high metabolic rate, not from the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 哺乳动物的体温来自高代谢率，而不是太阳。
senses.why: those traits are exactly what makes an animal mammalian, so the adjective can name the mechanism rather than the membership.
senses.whyCN: 正是这些特征使一只动物成为哺乳动物，形容词因此可以指机制本身，而不只是指身份。

senses.title: Of an Evolutionary Lineage
senses.definition: used of a branch of the mammalian family tree and the animals that sit on it
senses.definitionCN: 用于哺乳动物演化树上的一个支系以及该支系上的动物
senses.example: The mammalian line split from the reptile line long before the dinosaurs died out.
senses.exampleCN: 哺乳动物这一支在恐龙灭绝之前很久就与爬行动物一支分开了。
senses.why: every class is a branch on a tree, so the adjective can follow the branch through time and not merely through a checklist.
senses.whyCN: 每个纲都是演化树上的一根枝条，形容词因此能沿时间追踪这一支，而不只是对应一份名录。

senses.title: Of a Laboratory Model
senses.titleCN: 实验用哺乳动物模型的
senses.definition: used of a mammal bred and kept for experiments
senses.definitionCN: 用于为实验而饲养繁殖的哺乳动物
senses.example: The drug was cleared in a mammalian model before any human trial.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药在进入任何人体试验之前已在哺乳动物模型中获得通过。
senses.why: a model animal is valued precisely for sharing mammalian physiology with humans, so the class name becomes a quality label.
senses.whyCN: 模型动物之所以有价值，正因为它与人类共享哺乳动物的生理，纲名于是变成一种品质标签。

senses.title: Of a Regional Fauna
senses.definition: used of the mammals native to a particular region, taken together as one group
senses.definitionCN: 用于某一地区原生的哺乳动物整体
senses.example: The island's mammalian fauna is small because few species crossed the water.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的哺乳动物区系很小，因为越过水面的物种寥寥无几。
senses.why: a fauna is a collective noun for one class in one place, so the adjective marks both the class and the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 区系是某一纲在某一地点的集合名词，形容词因此同时标出类群与边界。

senses.title: Belonging to Mammalogy
senses.definition: relating to the study of mammals as an academic discipline
senses.definitionCN: 与以哺乳动物为研究对象的学科有关
senses.example: Her mammalian research began in a museum drawer of unlabelled skins.
senses.exampleCN: 她的哺乳动物学研究始于一抽屉没有标签的皮张。
senses.why: the discipline and its object share one root, so the adjective slides from the animal to the scholarship built around it.
senses.whyCN: 学科与其研究对象同出一根，形容词因此能从动物滑向围绕它建立的学术工作。

senses.title: Figurative Warmth
senses.titleCN: 比喻：哺乳动物式的温情
senses.definition: figurative, of care that is bodily, close and continuous, like a mother suckling her young
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指像母兽哺育幼崽那样贴身、持续、出于本能的照护
senses.example: The old house offered a mammalian sort of comfort, warm and slightly damp.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子给人一种哺乳动物式的舒适，温暖而略带潮气。
senses.why: the core image is one body kept warm against another, and that physical closeness is what the metaphor borrows.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个身体贴着另一个身体取暖，比喻借用的正是这份身体上的贴近。

intro.en: Mammalian joins mammal, the English shortening of Linnaeus's Mammalia, with the adjective suffix -ian. Mammalia itself was built from Latin mamma 'breast' plus a neuter plural ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mammalian 由 mammal 加形容词后缀 -ian 构成，而 mammal 是林奈所立 Mammalia 的英语缩略；Mammalia 本身由拉丁 mamma「乳房」加中性复数词尾构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mamma was the ordinary Latin word for the breast or teat, not a technical term; its deeper origin is not settled, and an onomatopoeic account has been proposed.
items.cn: mamma 是拉丁语中「乳房、乳头」的平常说法，并非术语；它更早的来源不确定，另有拟声说。

items.en: Linnaeus introduced Mammalia in 1758 as the class name for animals that suckle, choosing the breast rather than hair or womb as the defining feature.
items.cn: 林奈于一七五八年立 Mammalia 为这一纲的名称，选择「乳房」而不是毛发或子宫作为界定特征。

items.en: The ending -alia is a neuter plural of the same pattern as Reptilia; it marks a collective taxonomic group rather than a single animal.
items.cn: 词尾 -alia 是中性复数，与 Reptilia 等纲名同一模式；它标记集合性的分类群，而非单个动物。

items.en: English mammal is an eighteenth-century shortening of Mammalia, coined so that the class would have a singular noun like every other class.
items.cn: 英语 mammal 是十八世纪对 Mammalia 的缩略，造出它是为了让这一纲像其他纲一样有一个单数名词。

items.en: The suffix -ian comes from Latin -ianus and means 'belonging to, connected with', so mammalian means 'belonging to the mammals'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ian 来自拉丁 -ianus，意为「属于……、与……有关」，所以 mammalian 就是「属于哺乳动物的」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin ancestry of mamma is unknown and competing hypotheses are not settled here; the first date of mammalian as an English adjective is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：mamma 在拉丁语之前的来历不明，各种假说此处不选定论；mammalian 作为英语形容词的首见年代同样只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical shapes, two sharing the root mamma and two not. Group two holds words that overlap with mammalian in meaning but differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近的词，两个与 mamma 同根、两个不同根；第二组是含义重叠但范围不同的词。

entries.definition: Built on mamma plus -ary, it names the milk glands themselves rather than the class of animals.
entries.definitionCN: 由 mamma 加 -ary 构成，指乳腺本身，而不是动物类群。

entries.definition: The singular noun derived from Mammalia; mammalian is its adjective, so the two differ in part of speech rather than in root.
entries.definitionCN: 由 Mammalia 派生的单数名词；mammalian 是它的形容词，二者差别在词性而不在词根。

entries.definition: The extinct elephant takes its name from Russian mamont, whose own origin is uncertain; its resemblance to mamma is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 这种已灭绝的象得名于俄语 mamont，该词自身来源不确定；它与 mamma 的相似只是巧合。

entries.definition: An African snake named from Zulu; it contains no Latin element and shares only letters with mammalian.
entries.definitionCN: 一种非洲蛇，名字来自祖鲁语；其中没有拉丁成分，与 mammalian 只是字母相同。

entries.definition: Relating to the placental mammals, the largest subgroup of Mammalia; it is narrower than mammalian, which covers the whole class.
entries.definitionCN: 与有胎盘类哺乳动物有关，那是哺乳纲中最大的一支；它比 mammalian 窄，后者覆盖整纲。

entries.definition: Relating to the pouched mammals, and also a noun for one of them; it parallels mammalian but names a different branch.
entries.definitionCN: 与有袋类哺乳动物有关，也可作名词指其中一种；它和 mammalian 结构相仿，却指另一支。

entries.definition: An animal with a backbone; every mammal is a vertebrate, but most vertebrates are not mammals, so this word is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 有脊柱的动物；每只哺乳动物都是脊椎动物，但多数脊椎动物不是哺乳动物，因此这个词范围更宽。

entries.definition: Maintaining a constant body temperature; it describes a single mammalian feature rather than membership in the class.
entries.definitionCN: 维持恒定体温；它描述哺乳动物的一项特征，而非是否属于这一纲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root, the real Linnaean class name, and the real zoological phrases that fix each sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的林奈纲名，以及固定各个义项的真实动物学搭配。

normal.en: mamma 'breast' plus the neuter plural -alia made Mammalia; mammal is its English shortening, and -ian adds 'belonging to'.
normal.cn: mamma「乳房」加中性复数 -alia 构成 Mammalia；mammal 是它的英语缩略，-ian 再加「属于」。

normal.en: The class name chose the breast over hair or womb, which is why milk sits at the centre of the image.
normal.cn: 纲名选的是乳房而非毛发或子宫，乳汁因此位于意象中心。

normal.en: The same root runs through mammary, mammalogy, mammalogist and mammal.
normal.cn: 同一词根贯穿 mammary、mammalogy、mammalogist 与 mammal。

normal.en: Zoological phrases fix the senses: mammalian species, mammalian fauna, mammalian model, mammalian lineage.
normal.cn: 动物学搭配固定义项：哺乳动物物种、哺乳动物区系、哺乳动物模型、哺乳动物支系。

normal.en: Mammalians is the rare plural noun; the ordinary word for one animal is simply mammal.
normal.cn: mammalians 是罕见的复数名词，指一只动物时通常直接用 mammal。

abstract.en: Picture a mother's body curved around a smaller body, the two temperatures merging into one pocket of warmth.
abstract.cn: 想象母兽的身体弯成一道弧，把更小的身体裹进去，两个体温合成一袋暖意。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree whose branches are drawn as bodies rather than as lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵族谱，枝条不是线，而是一个个身体。

abstract.en: Picture a museum drawer of skulls, each labelled with the same class name whatever its size.
abstract.cn: 想象一只装满头骨的抽屉，不论大小都贴着同一个纲名。

examples.en: Mammalian red blood cells lose their nuclei before they mature.
examples.cn: 哺乳动物的红细胞在成熟之前就失去了细胞核。

examples.en: The fossil beds show a mammalian presence in the valley by the early Eocene.
examples.cn: 化石层显示，这座山谷在始新世早期已有哺乳动物存在。

examples.en: The team compared the mammalian immune response with that of birds.
examples.cn: 研究团队把哺乳动物的免疫反应与鸟类的作了比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈么连」——幼崽贴着母亲、连着乳汁的一类，就是哺乳动物。

root: 拉丁 mamma「乳房」+ 中性复数 -alia = 林奈一七五八年所立 Mammalia；英语 mammal 为其缩略，mammalian = mammal + -ian（拉丁 -ianus「属于」）。mamma 更早的来源不确定，另有拟声说，此处不选定论。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses radiate from one picture: a body that feeds and warms its young. From it come the taxonomic label, the countable animal, the defining physiology, the lineage, the laboratory stand-in, the regional fauna, the discipline, and finally the metaphor of bodily warmth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个画面发散：一个用乳汁喂养、用体温护住幼崽的身体。分类标签、可数的动物、界定性的生理、演化支系、实验室替身、地区区系、学科名，最后是身体温暖的比喻，都由此而来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mother's body feeding and warming a smaller body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个母体用乳汁和体温护住更小的身体。

branches.en: MEMBERSHIP: the class name yields both the adjective and the countable animal.
branches.cn: 归类：纲名同时产生形容词与可数的动物。

branches.en: DEFINING BODY: warm blood and milk define the class, and a whole regional fauna is described the same way.
branches.cn: 界定性的身体：温血与乳汁界定这一类，整个地区区系也用同样方式描述。

branches.en: LONG BRANCH: the class is a lineage in time and later an object of study.
branches.cn: 长枝：这一类既是时间上的支系，后来也成为研究对象。

branches.en: STAND-IN: a laboratory mammal carries the class into an experiment.
branches.cn: 替身：一只实验室哺乳动物把这一纲带进实验。

branches.en: BORROWED WARMTH: physical closeness becomes a metaphor for care.
branches.cn: 借来的温暖：身体上的贴近成为照护的比喻。

intro.en: Mammalian can be read in four pieces: a Latin noun for the breast, a neuter plural that turns it into a class name, the English shortening of that class name, and an adjective suffix.
intro.cn: mammalian 可以分四段读：表「乳房」的拉丁名词、把它变成纲名的中性复数词尾、该纲名的英语缩略，以及形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin mamma belongs to the first declension and gives the class name Mammalia; the same stem reappears in mammal, mammary and mammalogy, while -ianus supplies the English -ian.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mamma 属第一变格法，由此产生纲名 Mammalia；同一词干再现于 mammal、mammary 与 mammalogy，而 -ianus 提供英语的 -ian。

items.example: The root names the organ that defines the class.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名了界定这一纲的器官。

items.meaningCN: 哺乳纲，以哺乳为特征的动物纲
items.example: Linnaeus placed humans inside Mammalia.
items.exampleCN: 林奈把人类也放在哺乳纲之内。

items.example: Every mammal has hair at some stage of life.
items.exampleCN: 每只哺乳动物在生命的某个阶段都有毛。

items.example: The suffix turns the class noun into a descriptive adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把纲名变成描述性的形容词。

items.example: The adjective labels any trait or member of the class.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记该纲的任何特征或成员。

items.example: Mammary tissue enlarges before birth.
items.exampleCN: 乳腺组织在分娩前增大。

items.example: Mammalogy grew out of general zoology.
items.exampleCN: 哺乳动物学由普通动物学中分化而来。

items.example: The mammalogist sorted the skins by species.
items.exampleCN: 哺乳动物学家按物种把皮张分开。

items.example: Some extinct reptiles were mammal-like in their teeth.
items.exampleCN: 一些已灭绝的爬行动物牙齿似哺乳动物。

definition_zh: 探索性的；勘探的；试探性的
definition_en: intended to search out, investigate or test something whose outcome is not yet known
core_image: 一个人举着火把走进尚未绘制的洞穴，边走边把路线记在纸上
scene: 这里指「探索性的」。 The team ran an exploratory survey before committing money to the full excavation.
sceneCN: 这里 exploratory 是「探索性的、摸底性质的」（第 1 个义项：为了先弄清情况而做的调查）；句意：团队在投入全部开挖资金之前先做了一次探索性勘测。图中可辨识物件：火把、洞穴入口、测绘图、标记桩。

pos.zh: 探索性的；勘探的；试探性的

derivatives.zh: 探索性的（与 exploratory 近义，更少用）

senses.title: Searching out the unknown
senses.definition: done in order to find out what exists or what is happening, before any final decision is made
senses.definitionCN: 为了先弄清存在什么、正在发生什么而做的，尚未作出最终决定
senses.example: An exploratory visit to the site revealed two problems the report had missed.
senses.exampleCN: 对现场的一次探索性走访发现了报告漏掉的两个问题。
senses.why: explorare in Latin means 'to search out'. The -ory suffix marks a purpose, so an exploratory action exists for the sake of searching, not for the sake of a result.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 explorare 意为“搜出、查明”。-ory 后缀标记用途，所以 exploratory 的行为是为“查”本身而存在，不是为某个既定结果服务。

senses.title: Probing the ground
senses.titleCN: 勘探的：先打孔看看地下
senses.definition: relating to the search for oil, minerals or water under the ground
senses.definitionCN: 与寻找地下石油、矿产或水有关的
senses.example: Exploratory wells are cheap compared with the wells that actually produce oil.
senses.exampleCN: 与真正出油的井相比，勘探井的成本很低。
senses.why: Mining and oil use the same word because the search happens before extraction. The hole is a question, not yet an answer.
senses.whyCN: 采矿与石油业沿用同一个词，因为“找”发生在“采”之前。那个钻孔是一个问题，还不是答案。

senses.title: Tentative, not final
senses.titleCN: 试探性的：先走一步看反应
senses.definition: acting as a first cautious step whose results will decide whether to continue
senses.definitionCN: 作为谨慎的第一步、由结果决定是否继续的
senses.example: The company sent an exploratory email rather than a formal offer.
senses.exampleCN: 公司发了一封试探性的邮件，而不是正式报价。
senses.why: A tentative step keeps the door open. The word borrows the miner's caution: you test the ground before you build on it.
senses.whyCN: 试探性的一步保留了退路。这个词借用了矿工的谨慎：先试地下，再在上面动工。

senses.title: Medical probing
senses.titleCN: 探查性的：打开看看里面怎么了
senses.definition: describing surgery or a clinical trial carried out to find the cause or the safe dose
senses.definitionCN: 指为查明病因或安全剂量而进行的手术或临床试验
senses.example: Exploratory surgery showed that the pain came from a small adhesion.
senses.exampleCN: 探查性手术显示疼痛来自一处小的粘连。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the mining image directly: the body is opened to look, because scans have not explained enough.
senses.whyCN: 医学直接借用了采矿的意象：扫描没能解释清楚，于是打开身体去看。

senses.title: Learning by discovery
senses.titleCN: 探索式学习的：让学生自己找到答案
senses.definition: describing teaching in which learners investigate a question instead of receiving the answer
senses.definitionCN: 指让学习者自行探究问题、而不是直接接受答案的教学方式
senses.example: The exploratory lesson began with a question and no textbook page.
senses.exampleCN: 这堂探索式课程从一个问题开始，没有对应的课本页。
senses.why: Here the search moves inside the classroom: the student repeats the original act of finding out, and the finding is the lesson.
senses.whyCN: 这里“找”移到了教室内部：学生重复了最初那个“查明”的动作，而查到的过程本身就是课。

senses.title: Statistics: open-ended analysis
senses.titleCN: 探索性数据分析的：先看数据长什么样
senses.definition: in statistics, describing analysis that looks for patterns before a specific hypothesis is fixed
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上指在确定假设之前先寻找数据模式的分析
senses.example: Exploratory analysis found a cluster of outliers in the northern stations.
senses.exampleCN: 探索性分析在北部站点发现了一簇离群值。
senses.why: Exploratory data analysis reverses the usual order: instead of testing a guess, it lets the data suggest the guess, which is again a search outward.
senses.whyCN: 探索性数据分析颠倒了通常顺序：不是检验某个猜想，而是让数据提出猜想，仍然是向外搜找。

senses.title: First-round talks
senses.titleCN: 探索性会谈：先摸摸对方底线
senses.definition: describing early discussions whose purpose is to discover whether agreement is possible
senses.definitionCN: 指目的在于探明能否达成协议的早期磋商
senses.example: Exploratory talks resumed in Geneva after a three-month pause.
senses.exampleCN: 探索性会谈在中断三个月后于日内瓦重启。
senses.why: Diplomacy uses exploratory for talks that are not yet negotiations. Nothing is conceded; the only product is information.
senses.whyCN: 外交上用 exploratory 指还算不上谈判的会谈：不作让步，唯一的产出是信息。

senses.title: Testing the environment
senses.titleCN: 试探行为的：伸出一只脚试试水深
senses.definition: in animal and human behaviour, describing actions that gather information about a new setting
senses.definitionCN: 在动物与人类行为研究中，指为获取新环境信息而做的动作
senses.example: Exploratory behaviour in the young rats increased when the cage was new.
senses.exampleCN: 笼子换成新的时，幼鼠的探索行为增加了。
senses.why: Behavioural science keeps the physical image: an organism reaches out, touches, retreats, and maps the space by movement.
senses.whyCN: 行为科学保留了身体意象：生物伸手、触碰、退回，用移动把空间画成地图。

intro.en: Exploratory comes from Latin explorare 'to search out, investigate', built on ex- 'out' plus plorare 'to cry out'. The image is a hunter shouting while searching. English added -ory to make the adjective.
intro.cn: exploratory 来自拉丁语 explorare“搜出、调查”，由 ex-“向外”加 plorare“呼喊”构成。意象是猎人在搜寻时大声呼喊。英语加上 -ory 构成形容词。

items.en: plorare meant 'to cry out, wail'. Its further origin is uncertain; some scholars connect it with pluere 'to rain', but this is a guess and should be marked source uncertain.
items.cn: plorare 意为“大声喊、哭喊”。其更深来源不确定，有学者把它与 pluere“下雨”联系起来，但这只是推测，应标注“来源不确定”。

items.en: ex- 'out' plus plorare produced explorare, 'to cry out while searching', hence 'to search out, examine'. The shout is the signal that someone is looking.
items.cn: ex-“向外”加 plorare 构成 explorare，意为“一边搜寻一边呼喊”，引申为“搜出、检查”。喊声就是“有人在找”的信号。

items.en: explorator was a scout or spy, the person who went ahead to see what was there. The noun keeps the human agent of the search.
items.cn: explorator 是侦察兵、探子，先行去看情况的人。这个名词保留了“搜寻”的执行者。

items.en: English builds exploratory on the stem explorat- plus -ory, from Latin -orius 'serving for'. The adjective appears in the 17th century, first in religious and then in scientific writing.
items.cn: 英语以 explorat- 词干加 -ory（来自拉丁 -orius“用于……”）构成 exploratory。该形容词出现于 17 世纪，最早见于宗教写作，随后进入科学写作。

items.en: From the 19th century exploratory spreads to surgery, drilling and field surveys, where the search must happen before any commitment.
items.cn: 19 世纪起，exploratory 扩展到外科、钻探与野外勘测，这些场合都必须先搜寻、后投入。

items.en: In the 20th century the word reaches statistics and diplomacy, naming analysis and talks that deliberately avoid a fixed conclusion.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词进入统计学与外交领域，指刻意不预设结论的分析与会谈。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ex- or -plor- shape but not always the same root; the near-meaning group shares the idea of a first, cautious step.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ex- 或 -plor- 的外形，但未必同根；近义组都含“先走一步、谨慎试探”的意思。

entries.definition: another adjective from the same verb, meaning 'tending to explore'. It describes a quality, while exploratory describes a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词派生的另一形容词，意为“有探索倾向的”。它描述性质，而 exploratory 描述用途。

entries.definition: the act of searching or travelling to find out. The noun names the activity; the adjective names what the activity is for.
entries.definitionCN: 探索、勘探的行为。名词命名活动本身；形容词命名活动的用途。

entries.definition: taking unfair advantage of people or resources. It looks close because of ex- and -or-, but exploit comes from Latin explicare 'unfold', not from plorare.
entries.definitionCN: 剥削性的；利用他人或资源的。它因 ex- 与 -or- 而形近，但 exploit 来自拉丁 explicare“展开”，并非 plorare。

entries.definition: concerned with discovering facts, often formally. It stresses method and evidence, while exploratory stresses the open, unfinished stage.
entries.definitionCN: 调查性的；重在查明事实，常带正式色彩。它强调方法与证据，而 exploratory 强调开放、未定型的阶段。

entries.definition: coming before the main part as preparation. It marks order, not necessarily search.
entries.definitionCN: 初步的；作为主要部分之前的准备。它标记顺序，不一定含“搜寻”之意。

entries.definition: done or said in a cautious way, ready to be changed. It describes hesitation, while exploratory describes the information being sought.
entries.definitionCN: 试探性的；谨慎且可更改的。它描述犹豫，而 exploratory 描述被搜寻的信息。

entries.definition: used as an adjective for a small trial that tests whether a larger plan will work. It is close to exploratory but implies a planned full version to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 试点性的；以小规模试验检验更大计划是否可行。它接近 exploratory，但暗含之后有计划的完整版本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + plorare 'cry out': the explorer is the one who shouts outward while looking.
normal.cn: ex-“向外”+ plorare“呼喊”：探索者就是一边向外喊、一边找的人。

normal.en: exploration, explore and explorer all keep the same stem, so the family is learned as one block.
normal.cn: exploration、explore、explorer 共享同一词干，可以整块记忆。

normal.en: exploratory talks and exploratory drilling are both first steps that produce information, not final products.
normal.cn: exploratory talks 与 exploratory drilling 都是产出信息、不产出成品的第一步。

normal.en: exploratory surgery is literally opening the body to look, which is the clearest picture of the word.
normal.cn: exploratory surgery 字面上就是打开身体去看，是这个词最清楚的画面。

normal.en: The opposite situation is a confirmatory study, which tests a claim already fixed; exploratory looks before the claim exists.
normal.cn: 反面的情形是 confirmatory study（确证性研究），检验已经固定的主张；exploratory 则是在主张出现之前先看。

abstract.en: Think of a lantern sweeping across a cave wall: the beam does not build anything, it only shows what is there.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯扫过洞壁：光束不建造任何东西，只是把已有的东西照出来。

abstract.en: Think of a hand testing the temperature of water with one finger before the whole body enters.
abstract.cn: 想象先用一根手指试水温，然后整个身体才下水。

abstract.en: Think of a map that is still mostly blank, with a dotted line marking where someone has already walked.
abstract.cn: 想象一张大半空白的地图，只有一条虚线标出已经走过的路。

examples.en: The ministry funded an exploratory project to see whether the soil could hold a dam.
examples.cn: 该部门资助了一个探索性项目，看看这土壤能否承住一座水坝。

examples.en: After two exploratory meetings, both sides agreed to draft a real treaty.
examples.cn: 经过两次探索性会谈，双方同意起草一份正式条约。

examples.en: Exploratory analysis is useful precisely because it does not decide the answer in advance.
examples.cn: 探索性分析之所以有用，恰恰因为它不预先决定答案。

dict_mnemonic.text: “往外铺路”——ex（向外）+ plor（铺路的“铺”音近）：先向外铺一条小路，边走边看 → exploratory 探索性的

root: 拉丁 explorare“搜出、调查”（ex-“向外”+ plorare“呼喊”，plorare 的更深来源不确定）；explorat- 词干 + -ory“用于……的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one motion: a person moves outward into unmapped ground, and the moving itself is the point.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：人向外走进尚未绘图的地方，而“走”本身就是目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lantern moving into an unmapped cave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯移进尚未绘图的洞穴。

branches.en: SEARCH AND SURVEY: the general search and the miner's test hole are the same outward movement, one on land and one under it.
branches.cn: 搜寻与勘测：一般性探索与矿工的试孔是同一个向外动作，一个在地面，一个在地下。

branches.en: CAUTIOUS FIRST STEP: an exploratory email and exploratory talks both buy information before commitment.
branches.cn: 谨慎的第一步：试探性邮件与探索性会谈，都在投入之前先换取信息。

branches.en: MEDICAL PROBE: surgery that opens the body to look is the literal version of the same search.
branches.cn: 医学探查：为看清楚而打开身体的手术，是同一搜寻的字面版本。

branches.en: LEARNING: discovery-based teaching moves the search inside the learner, who repeats the original act.
branches.cn: 学习：发现式教学把搜寻移进学习者内部，让他重复最初的动作。

branches.en: OPEN-ENDED INQUIRY: data analysis and animal exploration both gather patterns before any hypothesis is fixed.
branches.cn: 开放式探究：数据分析与动物探索都在固定假设之前先收集模式。

intro.en: Exploratory is a Latin stem with the English suffix -ory. The ex- prefix is still readable as 'out', while -ory marks purpose; -tion and -er build the noun family.
intro.cn: exploratory 是拉丁词干加英语后缀 -ory。ex- 前缀仍可读作“向外”，-ory 标记用途；-tion 与 -er 构成名词族。

latinIntro.en: The family grows from plorare 'cry out' through explorare 'search out' to explorator 'scout'. The stem appears as explor- in English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 plorare“呼喊”经 explorare“搜出”生长到 explorator“侦察者”。英语中词干作 explor-。

items.meaningCN: 探索；勘探（ex-“向外”+ plorare“呼喊”）
items.example: They explored the cave for three days.
items.exampleCN: 他们花了三天探索那个洞穴。

items.meaning: the act of searching or surveying
items.meaningCN: 探索；勘探（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: Exploration of the seabed began last spring.
items.exampleCN: 海底勘探于去年春天开始。

items.meaningCN: 探索者；探险家（-er 构成施事名词）
items.example: The explorer mapped the river's upper course.
items.exampleCN: 这位探险家绘制了那条河的上游。

items.meaningCN: 有探索倾向的（-ive 表性质）
items.example: The study used an explorative design with open questions.
items.exampleCN: 该研究采用了带开放问题的探索性设计。

items.example: Much of the cave remains unexplored.
items.exampleCN: 洞中很大一部分仍未勘探。

items.example: The exploratory phase lasted six weeks.
items.exampleCN: 探索阶段持续了六周。

items.meaning: a scout or investigator, now rare
items.meaningCN: 侦察者；调查者（-or 施事名词，现罕用）
items.example: The old texts call the scout an explorator.
items.exampleCN: 古籍把侦察兵称作 explorator。

items.meaningCN: 以探索的方式（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: She asked the question exploratively rather than as a challenge.
items.exampleCN: 她以探索的口吻提问，而不是在挑衅。
